He was a cultivated man, eager to encourage younger talent and, particularly, free of prejudice between Manchus and Han Chinese.
此人很风雅，乐予奖掖后进，尤其是没有满汉的畛域之见。

The rear garden of his headquarters was renowned for its flowers and trees, and he often invited the city’s promising young scholars to gather there for literary conversation and wine.
将军署的后花园，颇有花木之胜，长善常常邀请广州的一班少年名士作文酒之会。

At the metropolitan examination in the gengchen year, two years before, Minister of Works Weng Tonghe had presided, allowing men of genuine learning to distinguish themselves.
前年庚辰科会试，闱中由工部尚书翁同齸主持，实学真才多能脱颖而出，

Liang Dingfen of Guangdong and Yu Shimei of Guangxi, both frequent guests of Changshan, had been selected for the Hanlin Academy.
其广东的梁鼎芬、广西的于式枚便常常作长善座上客，而且都点了翰林。

Zhang Shusheng’s son, Zhang Huakui, had also often received Changshan’s invitations while in Guangzhou.
在广州时，张树声的儿子张华奎，亦常受长善的招邀，

He was therefore a close friend of Yu and Liang, and of Wen Tingshi from Jiangxi, whose literary reputation surpassed theirs but who had unfortunately failed the metropolitan examination.
所以跟于式枚、梁鼎芬，还有一个文名盛於于、梁但禀表会试不幸落第的江西人文廷式。都是极熟的朋友。

Having accompanied his father to the governor-generalship of Zhili, Zhang Huakui now frequently visited the capital and spent time with these three friends.
这时张华奎随父到直隶总督任上，便经常进京，与于、梁、文等三人盘桓。


Though old friendships were warm and meeting familiar faces away from home was a pleasure, Zhang Huakui had another object.
虽说他乡遇故，旧雨情深，但张华奎却是另有企图。

In recent years, officials entitled to remonstrate had acquired immense influence.
原来这几年言路的势力极大，

The Hanlin scholars who also lectured to the throne were especially powerful: their words carried such weight that even the Empress Dowager Cixi and Prince Gong could not disregard them.
尤其是一班兼讲官的翰林，一言九鼎，连慈禧太后及恭王都不能不听，

These were the “Pure Stream,” the court’s moral critics; the four most famous were known as the Four Hanlin Remonstrants.
这班人就是『清流』，其中最有名的四个人，号为『翰林四谏』。

Yu Shimei and Liang Dingfen were junior Hanlin members, but their longstanding literary distinction brought them into frequent contact with these men.
于式枚、梁鼎芬虽是翰林后辈，但文名久著，所以亦常与清流有往还；

Through Yu and Liang, Zhang Huakui gained access to such leading critics as Zhang Peilun and Sheng Wu.
而张华奎便是凭借了于、梁的关系，得以上文张佩纶、盛吴这一班响当当大清流。

Zhang Huakui was a provincial graduate, young but capable, with a modest and agreeable disposition.
这张华奎是个举人，年纪虽轻，人很能干，而且赋性廉和可亲，

Moreover, the Beiyang branch office had accumulated substantial “public funds,” against which any expense incurred in entertaining metropolitan officials could be charged.
加以『北洋分所』积存的『公款』很多，凡是应酬京官，无不可以报销，

This gave his talents still greater scope.
使得张华奎愈发长袖善舞，

Wherever the critics met—at Songyun Hermitage, the Shrine of Former Worthies of the Capital Region, such celebrated places as Taoran Pavilion and Chongxiao Temple, or even the lodgings of male entertainers in the Eight Great Lanes—he provided their banquets.
清流们集会，不论是在松筠庵，还是『畿辅先哲寺』，或者陶然亭、崇效寺这些名胜之处，乃至于八大胡同『相公』的下处，筵宴所需，都是他来备办，

Whenever errands or arrangements were required, he willingly undertook them.
有事需要奔走联络，张华奎更是义不容辞，

Thus he acquired the nickname “the Green Ox’s Legs.”
因而得了个『青牛腿』的外号。


“Green ox,” qingniu, sounded like qingliu, “Pure Stream.”
『青牛』是清流的谐音。

Every household had its picture of the spring ox.
民间家家有『春牛图』，

Spring belonged to the east, the east to wood, and wood to the colour green; a green ox was therefore a spring ox.
春为东，东为木，木色青，所以『青牛』也就是春牛。

In these pictures the head, body, horns, ears, belly, tail, legs, and hooves were distinctly marked.
画春牛图时，头、身、角、耳、腹、尾、胫、蹄、部位分明。

Wits accordingly used the various parts to represent members of the Pure Stream.
因而好事者，用青牛的各部分，来形容清流中人，

The head was Li Hongzao, tutor to the Tongzhi emperor; his two followers named Zhang—Zhang Zhidong and Zhang Peilun—were the body and belly.
牛头是同治皇帝的师傅李鸿藻，他门下两张——张之洞、张佩纶是牛身、牛腹。

Others said Li Hongzao was Goumang, the deity driving the ox, and that Zhang Peilun was its head: no one could withstand those two horns, and anyone they struck suffered grievously.
也有人说，李鸿藻是驱牛的勾芒神，张佩纶才是牛头，因为他头上的一对角厉害不过，凡被触及，必受巨创。

Since Zhang Huakui did the running about for the critics, they called him the legs.
张华奎因为替清流效奔走之劳，所以名之为『腿』；

Some, however, said he was not qualified even for that: he was merely the Pure Stream’s boots, serving its legs.
但也有人说，他连『清流腿』都不够资格，只是『清流靴子』为『清流腿』服务而已。


Whether legs or boots, Zhang Huakui certainly attracted attention.
不管是『清流腿』还是『清流靴子』，张华奎很受人瞩目是事实。

He also incurred the hostility of Li Hongzhang’s followers, who accused him of disloyal ambitions.
不过因此而引起了李鸿章门下的敌视，认为他『图谋不轨』，

First, he constantly cultivated Weng Tonghe, who had always been at odds with Li Hongzhang.
第一是因为他常巴结翁同齸，而翁同齸一向是与李鸿章不睦，

Most of the Pure Stream, meanwhile, followed Li Hongzao, leader of the northern faction, whereas Weng was a leading figure of the southern faction; their political views had always differed.
同时清流多为北派领袖李鸿藻门下，而翁同齸是南派巨擘，对政事的见解，一向是有差异的；

Second, Zhang Huakui’s energetic courtship of the critics plainly aimed to build up his father’s reputation so that he could replace Li Hongzhang.
第二，张华奎拼命拉拢清流，显然是在为他父亲培养声名，目的是想取李鸿章而代之。

Embellished accusations of this kind reached Hefei continually.
这些加油添酱的谗言，不断传到合肥，

Secluded there in the ritual observances of mourning, Li himself began to grow suspicious.
在『闭门读礼』的李鸿章不由得也动了疑心。

His followers accordingly started planning to oust Zhang and bring Li back.
他的一班徒党，因而开始谋划逐张迎李之计，

Before long they found their opportunity.
不久便找到了可乘之机。


Zhang Peilun was full of learning and eager to put it to public use.
原来张佩纶满腹经纶，颇有用世之志，

Zhang Huakui therefore advised his father to follow Zuo Zongtang’s earlier example: Zuo had enhanced his own standing by petitioning for Yuan Baoheng’s services.
张华奎便向他父献计，仿照当年左宗棠奏调袁葆恒来提高本人声价的办法，

Why not request Zhang Peilun as assistant commissioner for Beiyang military affairs, with particular responsibility for the navy?
不妨奏调张佩纶『帮办北洋军务』，专门督办水师。

Once his father agreed, Huakui worked hard to persuade Zhang Peilun.
张树声同意以后，张华奎极力向张佩纶游尽；

The Beiyang fleet already possessed several ironclad warships; its scale was impressive and its prospects boundless.
那时产洋的水师，已拥有好几艘铁甲兵轮，规模壮阔，前程无量，

Zhang was greatly tempted and eventually consented.
张佩纶怦然心动，终于同意了。

News soon spread through Tianjin, Baoding, and elsewhere.
于是天津、保定等处，很快地传出消息，

It was also said that, once appointed, Zhang would institute sweeping reforms and impeach all “four intendants and eight brigade commanders.”
还说张佩纶帮办北洋军务后，将大加整顿，『四道八镇』，一律要参。

The governor-general of Zhili had four circuit intendants and eight brigade commanders under him; each brigade’s station was called a zhen.
直隶总督属下，有四名道员，八名总兵，总兵驻防之地称为『镇』；

The phrase thus denoted the province’s regular civil and military establishment.
四道八镇便是直隶文武官员的经制，

All these men had, of course, been appointed by Li Hongzhang.
当然全部都是李鸿章所派的。


At this critical moment, however, Zhang Shusheng and his son made a false move. They were overhasty and unfamiliar with the precedents governing court appointments.
不道在此要紧关头，张树声父子一则操之过急；二则不明京朝掌故，以至于走错了一步。

Provincial governors-general and governors could petition to have metropolitan officials transferred to their provinces, but not members of the Hanlin Academy.
原来封疆大吏，准许奏调京官到省任职，但不准奏调翰林。

The prohibition had been particularly strict under Qianlong.
这个禁例在乾隆年间更为严格。

Hanlin scholars who also served as daily lecturers and recorders of the emperor’s activities could be summoned to his presence at any time and knew his every word and action.
因为翰林如兼日讲起居注官，随传在皇帝身边，一言一动，无不深知；

They also had opportunities to read memorials and share in state secrets.
而且有机会看到各种奏章，参预国家机密，

Transferring them at a provincial chief’s request created a risk of disclosure; hence the strict rule.
如为疆吏所奏调，便有泄密之虞，因而有此厉禁。

Since the Taiping rebellion, enforcement had relaxed, but two questions still mattered: whether the petitioner had sufficient standing, and whether the appointment was truly necessary at that moment.
到得洪杨以后，禁例虽不如以前之严，但第一要看请奏调的人，够不够分量；第二要奏调的时机，是否确有需要。

When Zuo requested Yuan Baoheng to direct his supply administration, he was a distinguished commander honoured with a noble title and high ministerial rank, about to undertake a major western campaign in which Yuan’s assistance was essential.
当年左宗棠是封拜相的勋臣；奏调袁葆恒总理粮台，又有正当大举西征，用兵深资倚赖的理由，

Approval had naturally been easy to obtain.
自然容易照准。

Zhang Shusheng’s standing fell far short of Zuo’s, and there was no pressing military need.
如今张树声的资格远不如左宗棠，且亦非军务所必需，

When his memorial requesting Zhang Peilun reached the Grand Council, it was rejected by imperial order.
因而请奏调张佩纶的折子一到军机处，竟奉旨驳斥。

This sharp rebuff gravely damaged the governor-general’s prestige; for Zhang Peilun, it was still more humiliating.
这一下不但张树声以封疆大吏碰这么个硬钉子，大伤威望，张佩纶的面子更加难看。


Zhang Peilun considered himself worthy of being “the honoured guest of princes.”
照张佩纶的想法，他应该是『诸侯之上客』，

Zhang Shusheng ought to have treated him with the reverence of a pupil towards a master.
张树声应该北面以师礼相事，

Merely agreeing to assist with Beiyang military affairs had already seemed a concession.
如今答应帮办北洋军务，已嫌委屈；

If the governor-general truly wished to recruit him, he should have arranged matters with the Grand Council and secured a special imperial appointment to Beiyang, giving him the dignity he deserved.
张树声果然有心延揽，应该设法疏通军机，用『特旨』派他到北洋，才够面子。

Now the edict rebuked Zhang Shusheng for presumption.
加今上谕中责备张树声『冒昧』，

Presumptuous he certainly had been!
确是太冒昧了。

Li Hongzhang’s officials in Beiyang rejoiced at the rebuff.
李鸿章一系的北洋官僚，看到张树声碰钉子，自然高兴；

Hearing that Zhang Peilun had expressed resentment towards father and son, they were delighted beyond measure.
又听说张佩纶对张家父子有不满的表示，更是大喜过望，

Such an opportunity to divide them must not be lost.
认为挑拨离间的良机，决不可失。

It happened that, on the day Zhang Shusheng submitted his memorial, an examination was held for prospective provincial examiners.
恰好张树声上奏的那天有『考差』——

Metropolitan officials with provincial or metropolitan degrees had to pass it before being sent out to preside over provincial examinations.
两榜出身的京官，须经考试合格，才能放出去当乡试主考；

One such appointment could provide enough income for a year or two, so few men willingly missed the qualifying examination.
一任考官，所得可以维持一两年的生活，所以绝少有人放弃考差；

Zhang Peilun, however, was in mourning and ineligible for appointment; he therefore had no need to sit it.
但张佩纶因为有丧服在身，不能派任考官，考差自然不必参加。

Outsiders did not know this.
这个缘故，外人不会知道，

Malicious people could thus spread a rumour that he had deliberately stayed away, waiting at home for the edict approving Zhang Shusheng’s request so that he could set off for his new post.
因而别有用心者，就可以造他一个谣言，说他故意避考，在家等待准为张树声所请的上谕，以便走马上任。

The slander spread swiftly and widely.
这个中伤的谣言，传布得很快也很广；

His reputation for integrity suffered severely, and his humiliation turned to anger—naturally redirected at the Zhangs.
张佩纶的清誉大损，不免恼羞成怒，自然是迁怒到张家父子身上。


“Everyone knows how narrow-minded the Academician from Fengrun is.
『丰润学士的气量小是大家都知道的，

He will certainly take revenge.
他一定会复仇，

Zhang Zhenxuan has outsmarted himself and cannot possibly keep Zhili,” Sha said. “All that is needed now is a reason for Li Hongzhang to be recalled before completing his mourning.
张振轩弄巧成拙，直督一定保不住。』沙一心说∶『现在只是在一个可以让李合肥夺情回任的理由，

Once they find one, Zhang must hand over the office.”
这个理由一找到，张振轩就要交卸。』

This inside information was useful to Hu.
这段内幕，对胡雪岩很有用；

He had assumed that even if Li returned, it would be only after the twenty-seven months of parental mourning.
原以为李鸿章即会回任，也是父母之丧二十七个月以后的事，

Yet with a suitable reason, he could return at any time.
不过只要有理由，随时可以回。

Zuo ought therefore to accelerate his efforts to expel Li’s influence from Liangjiang.
照此看来，左宗棠想驱逐李鸿章在两江的势力，应该加速进行才是。

By now Sha’s craving for opium had been satisfied.
其时沙一心的瘾已过足，

Hu accompanied him to Fourth Miss Xiangyun’s rooms, where they drank merrily, passing the cups beneath the moon.
便由胡雪岩陪着到湘云老四妆阁中，飞觞醉月地闹了一回酒。

When Sha rose to leave, the other guests remembered that Hu and Gu were to accompany Zuo on an inspection of the arsenal early the next morning and also took their leave.
沙一心起身告辞，余客亦知胡雪岩与古应春第二天一早要左宗棠巡视制造局，都说要走，

Only Lin Maoxian stayed on for a “dry bed” at Fourth Miss Xiangyun’s.
只有林茂先在湘云老四那里『借干铺』。

“Sha Yixin is a useful man,” Hu told Gu on the way home. “You might keep in closer touch with him.
『沙一心这个人很有用，』在归途中，胡雪岩对古应春说∶『你以后不妨跟他多联络联络，

He knows the Huai Army and Beiyang well.
他对淮军及北洋的情形很熟，

We can ask him to make inquiries when necessary.”
有事可以请他打听。』

“That was my intention from the beginning.
『我的原意就是如此。

Leave it to me, Little Uncle.
小爷叔放心好了，

I shall arrange it.”
我会安排。』


The Jiangnan Arsenal stood at Gaochangmiao, on the Huangpu River outside Shanghai’s county town.
江南制造局在上海县城外，濒临黄浦江的高昌庙，

The site had once been wasteland, but since Zeng Guofan petitioned for the arsenal’s establishment, settlement had steadily increased.
本来是一片荒地，自从曾国藩奏请设制造局以后，人烟日起，

A gravel road led east to the town’s south gate.
造一条石子马路，东通县城南门。

That day, however, Zuo boarded a boat in front of his temporary headquarters behind the Temple of the Heavenly Empress and travelled straight down the Huangpu to the arsenal’s own landing.
不过左宗棠这天仍旧是在天前宫后辕前面下船，沿黄浦江直达制造局的专用码头，

Its director, the expectant circuit intendant Li Mianlin, received him in his large green-cloth sedan chair and conveyed him to the main hall.
制造局的总办，候补道李勉林用他的绿呢大轿，将左宗棠接到大堂，

There he presented his subordinate officers, who paid their respects in turn, before asking which section His Excellency wished to see first.
然后引见属员，一一参谒。接下来请示∶先看哪一处？

“The dockyard,” Zuo replied. “When I took leave of the throne last year, particular emphasis was laid upon maritime defence, and I was instructed to give it special attention.
『先看船坞吧』左宗棠说∶『我去年陛辞出京，上头特别交代，洋防要紧，要我分外留意。

Your dockyard may be smaller than Fujian’s, but it is nevertheless China’s second shipyard.
制造局的船坞，规模虽不及福建，到底是中国第二个造船厂，

If its men, grounds, and materials are all put to their fullest use, it can contribute substantially to our coastal defences.”
能人尽其用、地尽其用、物尽其用，对洋防亦颇有裨益。』

This opening address carried a hint of reprimand.
这一段开场白，便有些教训的意义，

Li Mianlin was naturally uncomfortable, and his embarrassment showed.
李勉林听入耳中，当然不很舒服，脸上不免有尴尬之色，

Hu intervened with a few words in Li’s favour and managed to smooth the occasion over.
见此光景，胡雪岩便在一旁替李勉林说好话，总算将场面圆过来了。


The dockyard was in such confusion that Zuo could make little of it.
船坞中乱糟糟一片，看不出一个名堂来，

He had to ask directly. “Grand Guardian Peng spends the year inspecting the Yangtze’s estuary and its river and sea defences.
左宗棠只好问了∶『彭宫保整年巡阅长江海口、江防、洋防的形势，

He has surveyed every aspect and written to me expressing concern that there are too few warships to meet our needs.
周览无遗，写信给我，以兵船不敷调度为虑，

He says at least ten small steamers must be added.
说至少要添造小火轮十号，

I think even ten are insufficient; it would be better to build five vessels on the latest fast-ship model as well.
照我看，十号亦还不够，最好再能仿造新式快船五艘，

Can you construct them here?”
你看你这里能不能造？』

“We can build small steamers.
『小火轮能造，

The new fast vessels are beyond the capacity of our machinery.”
新式快船，限于机器，力所不逮。』

“Then how much would each small steamer cost?”
『那末，造小火轮每一号要多少钱呢？』

“We should have to prepare an estimate.”
『这要估起来看。』

Again the conversation threatened to become awkward.
话又有些碰僵了，

Fortunately Zuo took no offence, asking only how long the estimate would require.
幸好左宗棠没有在意只问∶『要多少日子才能估得出来？』

“For accuracy, we should still have to consult the Fujian Naval Dockyard.
『估价欲求精确，还得找福建船政局，

They have complete plans and fuller information on material prices.
他们那里图说全备，材料的行情也比较准。

If Your Excellency is determined to proceed, we shall send someone to Fujian at once.
大人如果决意要造，局里马上派人到福建，

The detailed figures should be ready in about a month.”
大概有一个月的工夫，细帐就可以出来了。』

“Very well.
『好！

Please see to it immediately.”
请你马上就办。

Beside the dockyard stood the arms factory, which greatly interested Zuo.
『船坞旁边就是枪炮厂，左宗棠对这里很感兴趣，

His western campaigns had owed much to superior equipment, and he was particularly knowledgeable about foreign rifles.
因为西征，得力就在器械精良；尤其是对洋枪，他已经很内行了，

Yet for all his experience of seeing and using them, this was his first opportunity to observe their manufacture.
但看得多，用得多，洋枪如何制成，却还是初次见识，

Beginning with the steelworks, he inspected every department closely.
所以从炼钢厂看起，每一部门都看得很仔细。


At last they reached the inspection section, which had a firing range attached.
最后到了检验处，附设有个靶场，

Shots cracked noisily.
乒乓乒乓地声音很热闹。

As Zuo entered, an old man jumped down from a high stool and retreated to one side.
左宗棠一踏了进去，坐在高凳上的一个老头子跳了下来，躲到一边；

“Master Yao,” Li Mianlin called, “come and pay your respects to His Excellency Zuo!”
李勉林便喊∶『姚司务，见见左大人！』

Yao’s face was red as fire and his hair white as silver.
这姚司务面红似火，发白如银，

His eyes differed in size; the larger, the right, shone brightly.
一双眼一大一小，大的那只右眼，炯炯有神；

His arms were likewise mismatched, one thick and the other thin.
手臂亦是一粗一细，侔不相伦。

Zuo had seen much of the world and encountered many unusual people, but Yao’s singular appearance caught his attention at once.
左宗棠平生阅历甚富，看过不少异人；一看这姚司务形相古怪，不由得便加了几分注意。

When the old man had risen from his kowtow, Li said, “Master Yao is one of the arsenal’s treasures.
等姚司务磕过一个头起身，李勉林便看着左宗棠说∶『这姚司务是制造局一宝，

Any rifle that passes through his hands is certain to shoot true.”
不管什么枪，经他手里出去的，「准头」一定好。』

Ordnance was Zuo’s keenest interest.
『喔，』左宗棠对军械的兴趣最浓，

Looking up, he asked, “Is this where you test the rifles?”
当下抬起头来，看了一下问∶『这就是你验枪的所在？』

“Yes,” Li answered for Yao.
『是。』李勉林代为回答。

“How do you test them?”
『怎么验法？』

“Your Excellency may find it hard to believe.
『说起来大人恐怕不信，

He takes one look down the sights and fires one shot; then he knows.”
他只是瞄一眼、开一枪就知道了。』

“That is extraordinary skill!” Zuo said with pleasure. “I should like to see it.”
『这倒是神乎其技了。』左宗棠欣然说道∶『我倒要见识见识。』

“Certainly.”
『是。』

Li turned to Yao. “Give His Excellency a demonstration.”
李勉林转脸对姚司务说∶『你演练演练给大人看。』


Yao seemed so inarticulate that he could not even say yes.
姚司务似乎很木讷，连一声『是』都不会答应，

He merely nodded and moved the high stool away, intending to test the rifles standing up.
只点一点头去掇开那张高凳，意思是站着验枪。

“No, no!”
『不，不！』

Zuo stopped him hastily.
左宗棠急忙阻止，

“Do as you normally do.
『你照平常一样。

If you usually sit, sit now.”
平常坐着，现在不是坐着。』

Yao dared make no response.
姚司务不敢答应，

Li had to tell him, “Do as His Excellency instructs.”
仍旧须李勉林说一声∶『你照大人的吩咐。』

Only then did Yao replace the stool, climb its attached steps, and sit down.
姚司务这才又将高凳搬回原处，踩着凳上所附的踏级，坐了上去。

Before him, walls enclosed a long, narrow passage.
他面前是用墙砌出来的，狭长的一条弄堂，

At its far end stood a target of six concentric circles, its centre riddled with bullet marks.
尽头处是个六个同心圆的靶子，中心弹痕累累；

Yao called loudly, “A new target!”
姚司务便大声喊道∶『换个靶！』


Someone behind the target attended to it, and a fresh one appeared immediately.
枪靶后面有人在照料，顿时换了新靶。

Zuo noticed two long wooden chests on Yao’s left and two large baskets on his right, with rifles heaped carelessly inside.
左宗棠看他左面摆着两个长木箱，右面又有两个大箩筐，里面乱堆着枪枝，

The long chests held newly repaired rifles, tended by another man.
长木箱中是刚修好的枪，有个人在照管。

“Here!” Yao called.
『来！』听得姚司务这一声，

The attendant took a rifle and tossed it up to him.
那人便取一枝枪，抛了上去，

Yao caught it in his left hand, transferred it to his right, and narrowed his eyes for a glance.
姚司务左手接住，交到右手，眯起眼睛看了一下，

A shot rang out, followed almost immediately by a thump: he had thrown the rifle into the nearer basket.
便即听得『砰』的一声；接着又听得『彭』的一声，那枝枪已被他扔在前面那个箩筐里了。

Zuo had not even seen clearly how he pulled the trigger with one hand.
左宗棠根本没有看清楚，他是如何单手在扣扳机，

The little hole in the exact centre of the new target, however, was plain enough.
不过新靶上正中红心有个小洞，却看得很清楚。



胡雪岩 · 萧瑟洋场
The Desolate Foreign Settlement
第三章（本章第2部分，共4部分）
逐句英中对照
原著：高阳


Now came a rapid succession of cracks and thumps.
听这时又是『砰砰彭彭』好一阵，

Some rifles went into the outer basket and others into the inner one, though far fewer went into the outer.
有的枪丢在外面箩筐，有的枪丢在里面箩筐，不过外面少，里面多。

“Those in the outer basket have not been properly repaired and must go back,” Li Mianlin explained.
『是这样，』李勉林为左宗棠解释，『丢在外面的，没有修好，拿回去重修；

“Those in the inner one are ready.”
丢在里面的，是修好了的。』

Zuo was not entirely convinced.
左宗棠有些不大相信，

“One glance and one shot, and he can tell by the sound?
『就这么看一眼、放一枪，就能听得出来？』

It seems scarcely credible.”
他说∶『似乎有点不可思议。』

“Indeed it does, but that is how he does it.”
『是！是有点不可思议，不过确实如此。』

“There is something I do not understand.”
『我倒有点不明白。』

During a pause, Zuo called, “Master Yao!
左宗棠便趁空隙喊道∶『姚司务！

Master Yao!”
姚司务！』

The old man did not stir, as though he had heard nothing.
那姚司务纹风不动，恍若未闻，

Li hastened to explain.
李勉林赶紧又解释，

“He is hard of hearing.
『他重听，

Gunfire has damaged his eardrums.
耳鼓让枪声震坏。

In ordinary conversation he watches people’s lips.”
平时说话，只看人的嘴。』

He stepped forward, tapped Yao on the back, and signalled him to come down.
接着他走上前去，拍一拍姚务的身后，让他下来。


“How old are you, Master Yao?” Zuo asked.
『姚司务，』左宗棠问∶『你今年多大？』

“Sixty-six.”
『六十六岁。』

“How many years have you been handling guns?”
『你玩枪玩了少年了？』

Yao counted on his fingers. “Forty-eight.”
姚司务屈指算了一下∶『四十八年。』

Zuo made a quick calculation of his own. “Then you were already in this trade during the Daoguang reign?”
左宗棠也在心里略为算了一下说∶『这么说，你在道光那年就干这一行了？』

“Yes.”
『是。』

“Who taught you?”
『你跟谁学的？』

“First a German, then an Englishman.”
『先是德国人，后来是英国人。』

“And which guns do you think better, German or English?”
『喔！』左宗棠问∶『你说德国的枪好，还是英国的枪好？』

“German.”
『德国。』


Zuo turned to look behind him.
听这一说，左宗棠便回身去看，

Knowing whom he sought, Hu pushed forward through the crowd of officials.
胡雪岩知道是找他，便从一大堆官员中挤上前去。

“Xueyan, has Focke come?”
『雪岩，』左宗棠问道∶『福克来了没有？』

“No.
『没有。』

Have you any instructions for him, Your Excellency?
胡雪岩问∶『大人有什么吩咐？

I shall pass them on at once.”
我马上告诉他。』

“I want one of those Winchester rifles.”
『我是要找一枝「温者斯得」的枪。』

“I have already issued them to the recruits.
『呃，』胡雪岩答说∶『我已经分派给新兵，

They are using them.”
在用了。』

“Good.
『好、好！

Bring one here.”
拿一枝来。』

The rifle was placed in Yao’s hands, and he was asked whether he had seen one before.
这枝枪是交到姚司务手里，问他见过没有？

He had not.
答说没有。

Yet after a brief examination, he turned a screw and began removing the parts one by one.
不过他只略为看了一下，便转开一个螺丝，接着一样一样拆了下来，

In a few minutes, the new rifle lay in pieces.
不过几分钟的工夫，一枝新枪成了一堆零件。

This was genuine skill, and Zuo could not withhold his admiration.
这显出真工夫来了，左宗棠不能不服他，

“Is it a good rifle?” he asked.
当下问道∶『这枪好不好？』

Yao gave no answer, merely looking at Li Mianlin.
那姚司务竟不回答，只看着李勉林。

Zuo did not understand, but Hu did.
左宗棠不知是怎么回事；胡雪岩却看出来了，

If Yao pronounced it good, Zuo might immediately order rifles of that kind, cutting off the purchasing officers’ opportunities for profit.
姚司务一说好，左宗棠说不定马上就会交代购买那一种。那一来，岂不断了采购委员的财路。

Hu therefore remarked, “Perhaps it is not so good.”
因此，胡雪岩便说一句∶『只怕不见得好。』


Unexpectedly, Li took the opposite line.
谁知李勉林恰好相反，

“Good, good—excellent!” he repeated.
连连说道∶『好，好，好得很。』

On the surface they were being polite; in reality, they were already crossing swords and regarding one another with suspicion.
表面彼此客气，实际上已等于短兵相接，也是彼此猜忌。

The Jiangnan Arsenal was Li Hongzhang’s exclusive preserve.
本来江南制造局是李鸿章的禁脔，

Whether weapons were manufactured there or purchased abroad, Hu had no part in the business.
不管自造也好，外购也好，都轮不到胡雪岩来插手，

His remark that the rifle might not be so good therefore signalled that he did not intend to compete for the arsenal’s trade.
所以他之说『怕不见得好』，便有不愿跟制造局『抢生意』的意味在内；

Conversely, if he chose to compete, that trade was within easy reach.
反过来说，他如果要『抢生意』，唾手可得。

Li Mianlin felt keenly that a formidable rival stood before him and that caution was necessary.
这就使李勉林深深感到，劲敌当前，必须小心了。

The purchase of these Winchester rifles did, naturally, come Hu’s way.
这笔买『温者斯得』来福枪的生意，自然还是归胡雪岩，

The man who profited handsomely, however, was Focke.
但大发利市的却是福克。


Focke’s firm held the Chinese agency for these rifles.
原来这种枪的在华代理权，属于福克的洋行，

Of the first five hundred imported, barely more than a hundred had been sold despite efforts in every direction.
第一批进了五百枝，四处兜销，只卖去一百多，

He had not initially thought of Zuo, knowing that the western armies already had many rifles; Zuo had even sent a consignment to Prince Chun for use by the Shenji Battalion.
起初亦并未想到左宗棠，因为他知道西征军中来福枪极多，左宗棠甚至还送了一批给醇王，供神机营使用。

Hearing that Hu was coming to Shanghai, however, Focke thought Zuo’s personal detachment might need these superior new weapons and sent twenty as samples.
及至听说胡雪岩要到上海，心想左宗棠的『小队』也许要用这种比较精良的新枪，送了二十枝当样品，

Even if this produced an order, he expected no more than a hundred or so.
估量着，即使能做到这笔生意，充其量也不过百把枝，

Half his original stock would still remain, with no buyer in sight.
库存还有一半，不知销场何在？

Then word came through Hu: Zuo wanted two thousand five hundred, to be distributed among the various Jiangnan garrisons.
哪知由胡雪岩转来的消息，说要买两千五百枝，预备分发江南各防营使用。

Focke was delighted, but troubled as well.
福克喜出望外，却又发愁，

The goods available for immediate delivery did not amount even to the odd five hundred.
因为能够供应的现贷，连个零头都不足。

“Mr Hu,” he said through Gu’s interpretation, “I shall deliver what I have in stock first and supply the rest within three months.
『胡先生，』福克透过古应春的翻译，向胡雪岩说∶『我拿库中存货先交，其余的，准备三个月内交齐；

I shall go home myself expressly to arrange it.”
我回国去一趟，专门办这件事。


Hu discussed this with Gu.
胡雪碉便跟古应春商量，

He too had seen how wary Li Mianlin was of him.
他亦看出李勉林对他深具戒心，

It would be unwise to make an enemy at the outset and encounter increasing obstacles thereafter.
认为不宜一开始就树敌，免得以后的障碍愈来愈多。

Since Zuo had personally ordered these arms, he could hardly refuse to act; yet he feared Li’s resentment.
这笔军火是左宗棠亲自交代，不能不办；正愁着李勉林会『吃味』，

Focke’s insufficient stock offered a convenient reason to abandon the transaction and avoid offending Li.
难得福克供应不足，恰好打消了这笔生意，避免得罪李勉林。

He explained this to Gu.
他将他的意思告诉了给古应春，

“We had better turn it down now.
又说∶『我看就此推掉为妙。

Tell him the rifles are needed immediately.
你跟他说，马上要用，

We must have them in stock, or there is nothing to discuss.”
要现货，没有现货就免谈了。』

“He will not accept that explanation.
『这话他不会相认的。』

He knows how much influence you have with His Excellency.
古应春说∶『小爷叔在左大人面前讲话的分量，他不是不知道，

Arms purchases always begin with samples; if they are approved, an order follows.
哪一次买军火都是先送样品，看中意了再下定单，

To insist now that the entire quantity be available at once would plainly be making difficulties for him.”
如今说全部都要现货，不是明明为难他？』

“That is true.”
『这话倒也是。』

Hu hesitated. “Then let him see His Excellency himself.
胡雪岩踌躇了一会说∶『这样，你叫他自己去看左大人。

To avoid any suspicion, have him first visit Intendant Li at the arsenal and ask Li to take him to His Excellency.
而且我们要避嫌疑，你叫他先到制造局去看李观察，请李观察带他去见左大人。

Whether he secures the business will depend on his luck.”
生意成不成，看他自己的运气。』

“Will that work?” Gu asked doubtfully.
『这办法！行得通吗？』古应春不免怀疑，

“We need not hand our own connections over to someone else.”
『我们犯不着把自己的路子，交给人家。』

“No.
『不！

They are so afraid of us and so much on their guard that it would be foolish to make a sworn enemy over this small matter.
现在他们怕我们防得厉害，犯不着为这点小事，做成个死对头。

A little generosity now will make future business easier.”
不如现在大方一点，以后办事反而顺手。』

Gu reflected that giving now in order to gain later was a legitimate tactic.
古应春心想，这是欲取姑予的手法，亦未尝不可用。

The commission on two thousand five hundred rifles would be at least five thousand taels—a large sum to others, but a trifle to Hu.
两千五百枝枪的佣金，虽至少有五千佣金，别人看来是个大数目，但在胡雪岩眼中，却是小事；

Since he wished to be generous, Gu would do as he asked.
既然他要『大方』，就照他的意思办好了。


Focke could have no knowledge of Hu’s anxieties or calculations.
但胡雪岩的顾虑与打算，福克是怎么样也无从知道的，

He was bewildered by Gu’s message.
因此一听古应春的话，大感困惑，

After so many years of successful cooperation, why this rejection?
多年合作得好好地，何以有这种见拒的态度？

Had Hu lost his influence with Zuo, or was there some other reason?
莫非胡雪岩在左宗棠面前，说话已经没有力量了，还是另有其他原因？

He questioned Gu frankly.
当下率直向古应春发问。

Unable to tell him the truth, Gu said only that Hu wished to respect the Jiangnan Arsenal’s position.
古应春当然不能跟他说实话，只说胡雪岩是尊重江南制造局。

Focke half believed him.
这话在福克半信半疑，

After many years in China, he understood official life fairly well: whoever had the means could contend for power and profit.
他在华多年，官场中的情形，亦相当了解，向来是谁有办法，谁就可以争权夺利；

Authority and responsibility were ill-defined; talk of respect was still less credible.
权责并不分明，尊重更是假话。

An experienced operator, Focke first inquired into Hu’s standing with Zuo and learned that he had certainly not fallen from favour.
福克做事很老练，先去打听胡雪岩在左宗棠那里的『行情』，所得到的答复是绝未失宠。

He therefore began to suspect that someone else was trying to supplant him in the arms trade, and that Hu meant to discourage him into withdrawing.
这一来，他就不能不怀疑，另有人在钻军火生意的路子，想取他而代之；胡雪岩是一种让他知难而退的态度。

Gu denied this absolutely.
去问古应春，古应春绝口否认。

Focke then felt reassured.
这一下，福克释然了，

Chinese officialdom had many complications that could not be explained to foreigners; there was no need to investigate them all.
中国官场不足跟外人道的花样很多，不必去多打听。

In any event, he could not go wrong by holding to his principle of sharing profits, keeping Hu close, and preserving their longstanding cooperation.
反正自己仍旧抱定利益均沾的宗旨，将胡雪岩拉紧了，保持了多年合作的关系，总是不错的。


Focke therefore took an interpreter to the arsenal to see Li Mianlin.
于是福克便带了一名翻译到制造局求见李勉林。

Officials gave foreigners special treatment in those days, and Focke was one of Shanghai’s leading foreign merchants.
那时的官场，对洋人都是另眼看待，何况福克是上海洋商领袖之一，

As soon as his card arrived, Li left the guests he was receiving in the garden reception room and met him in his private office.
所以名刺一报进去，正在花厅中会客的李勉林，丢下他人，在签押房接见福克。

Asked his business, Focke explained through the interpreter: “His Excellency Zuo wishes to purchase two thousand five hundred Winchester rifles.
动问来意，福克透过翻译说道∶『左大人要买两千五百枝温者斯得来福枪，

I have only three hundred and some in stock, but can guarantee delivery of the rest within three months.
可是我现货只有三百多枝，其余准三个月内交足。

Intendant Hu says that will not do and has sent me to ask you to take me to His Excellency so that I may discuss it with him in person.”
胡观察说不行，要我来见李观察，请你带我去见左大人当面谈。』

Li was surprised.
听得这话，李勉林不免诧异，

Foreign arms were normally ordered for future delivery.
定购西洋军火，向来都是期货；

With no present disturbance at home or abroad, and no formidable enemy in battle requiring superior weapons urgently, why insist on immediate availability?
目前内外无事，又不是打仗遇到劲敌，急需要精良武器才足以克制，何必一定非现货不可？

Reflection made the answer plain: Hu did not wish to handle the purchase.
仔细想一想，显然是胡雪岩不愿意经手这件事，

Why not?
但又为什么不愿意呢？

There could be only one explanation. Zuo was no longer commander of the western expedition; he was governor-general of Liangjiang and commissioner for the Southern Ports.
唯一的缘故是左宗棠已非西征统帅，而是两江总督、南洋大臣，

The “jiang” and “nan” in those titles unmistakably indicated that this business belonged to the Jiangnan Arsenal.
两个头衔中一『江』、『南』，就彰明较著地表明了，这一案应该由江南制造局主办。

Li admired Hu’s respect for the proper boundaries.
对于胡雪岩的能守分际，李勉林颇为佩服，

Hu’s methods might be formidable, but he understood how things should be done.
胡雪岩的手腕很厉害，但还是『上路的』。


“Certainly!” Li answered readily.
当下欣然答说∶『可以、可以！

“His Excellency leaves for Jiangning tomorrow.
左大人明天动身回江宁，

I was going to see him in any case.
我本来就要去见他；

We can go together.”
我们一起去好了。』

They arranged to meet at three that afternoon at Zuo’s headquarters in the Temple of the Heavenly Empress.
于是约定当天下午三点钟，在天后宫行辕见面。

Once they had assembled there, Li sent in his card and was received first.
到时候会齐李勉林先递书本谒见，

At a suitable pause, he mentioned that Focke was waiting outside and had something to discuss in person.
然后找个谈话的空隙，说福克在外，等候接见，有事面禀。

Hu had already reported to Zuo and argued that having the arsenal handle the transaction would make the contract, payments, and other formalities more convenient. Zuo approved this reasoning and immediately admitted Focke.
左宗棠已经接到胡雪岩的报告，认为胡雪岩所说，此案由江南制造局承办，一切签约、付款等等手续，都比较方便的看法不错，所以听得李勉林的话，立即接见福克。

He knew him well and appreciated his orderly way of doing things, so his greeting was warm and gracious.
他跟福克很熟，也很欣赏福克的有条理，温言相接，颇假以词色；

He also agreed readily to the proposed arrangement: the available rifles would be delivered first, and the remainder in instalments by a fixed deadline.
谈到买枪一事，也很爽快的答应了，先交若干现货，余数立定期限，陆续解交。

Focke and Li were to settle the price between them.
价格方面，福克与李勉林细谈。


“These two thousand five hundred rifles are for the Green Standard troops,” Zuo instructed Li. “As soon as you receive them, hand them over to Li Chaobin.”
『这两千五面枝枪是交绿营用的。』左宗棠交代李勉林∶『你收到枪，马上交给李朝斌好了。』

Li Chaobin was the Jiangnan commander-in-chief, the highest officer of the Green Standard forces.
李朝斌的官衔是江南提督，绿营的最高长官。

“Yes, Your Excellency.”
『是。』

Zuo turned to Focke. “I hear you are going home. When do you leave, and when will you return?”
『听说你要回国。』左宗棠转脸问福克∶『什么时候动身，什么时候回来？』

“In ten days.
『十天以后动身，

I shall be back in two months.”
两个月就回来。』

“I now intend to reorganize the navy.
『我现在要整顿水师；

Torpedoes are an effective naval weapon, are they not?”
水师的利器，是鱼雷不是？』

“They are.”
『是的。』

“I should like to purchase a consignment.
『我想买一批鱼雷，

Can you supply them?”
你有没有？』

“Certainly.
『有、有。』

As Your Excellency knows, whenever a new weapon appears in any country, East or West, samples and instructions are sent to my firm.
福克答说∶『左大人知道的，东西洋各国凡有新出的利器，一定把样品跟说明书，送到我洋行里来的。

On this journey home, I can personally inquire into the newest models and bring them out.”
尤其是这趟我回国，可以亲自打听到最新式的运了来。』

“Could you bring technicians as well?”
『能不能连技师一起请了来。』

“Of course.
『当然。

Whenever China buys a new weapon it has not used before, technicians are always sent to demonstrate its operation.
凡是采购中国从前所没有的新式武器，一定由技师派来，教导如何演放。

That is an established practice; there will be no difficulty.”
这是必有的规矩，不会错的。』

“You have misunderstood me.
『喔，你没有弄清我的意思，

I mean technicians who can manufacture torpedoes.”
我是说能制造鱼雷的技师。』

“They can be found too, but we must first see whether the arsenal has suitable machinery.”
『那也有。』福克答说∶『不过要先看制造局，有没有能造鱼雷的机械。』

“Discuss that with Intendant Li.” Zuo continued, “There is also something called a ‘contact mine.’
『你跟李观察商量。』左宗棠又问∶『还有种「碰雷」，

What is that used for?”
作何用处？』


“It is—” Focke first clarified the term with his interpreter.
『是——』福克向翻译弄清楚了『碰雷』二字的意思，

“That is a naval mine, used specifically against enemy warships.
方始回答∶『那叫水雷，是专门为了防备对方兵舰用的。

For example, if you wish to keep their vessels out of a harbour, you can lay mines across its entrance.
譬如一个港口，不愿意对方舰闯进来，就可以在港口海面上布下水雷，

A ship touching one causes it to explode.”
船一碰到就会爆炸。』

“What about our own ships?”
『自己的船呢？』

“They would cause an explosion too.
『自己的船，一样也会爆炸。』

Mines are very powerful, but unfortunately they cannot distinguish friend from foe.
福克又说∶『水雷的威力很大，麻烦是不长眼睛，

They are therefore not used unless war with a foreign country makes it necessary to close the waterways.”
所以非遇到与外国交锋，打算断绝水路交通，不用水雷。』

“And afterwards?”
『事后呢？』

“Afterwards they must be cleared.
『事后要清理。

There is a special kind of vessel called a minesweeper.”
专门有种船叫扫雷艇。』

“Then the matter has wide implications.
『照此说来，这件事牵涉很广，

We shall leave it aside for now.
暂作罢论，

Simply obtain the latest torpedoes for China.
你只管替中国采购最新式的鱼雷好了。

Discuss the details with Intendant Li.”
细节你跟李观察去商议。』

“Yes, Your Excellency.”
『是！』

There seemed nothing more to say.
看看没有话了，

Prompted by the interpreter, Focke rose and took his leave.
福七克在翻译示意之下，起身告辞。

Li was asked to remain, but he had not been able to get a word into the entire conversation and was deeply displeased.
李勉林虽被留了下来，但从头到底没有能容他说一句话，内心万分不悦。


Zuo had kept Li behind to discuss something partly public and partly private.
至于左宗棠将李勉林留了下来，是要谈半公半私的事。

The private interest was not his own, however; it concerned Zeng Guofan’s youngest son-in-law, Nie Guiji.
不过私事倒也不是他的个人之私，是为了曾国藩的小女婿聂规缉。

Zeng’s wife, Madam Ouyang, had borne three sons and six daughters.
原来曾国藩的欧阳夫人，共生三子六女。

The first son and fifth daughter died in childhood, leaving two sons and five daughters.
长子及五女，自幼夭折；在世的有两子五女，

The elder surviving son, Jize, excelled both in letters and in public affairs.
长子纪泽，文章政事俱是第一流，

He had also taught himself English, which greatly pleased his father.
而且由自修而通英文，为国藩所看重，

Later he inherited the marquisate and went to the West as an imperial envoy.
后来袭封侯爵，以钦差大臣出使西洋，

He and Guo Songtao were men of exceptional ability who truly understood foreign affairs.
与郭嵩焘都是真正懂洋务的大才。

The younger son, Jihong, passed the provincial examination but repeatedly failed at the metropolitan level.
次子纪鸿中举以后，会试一直不利；

Zeng knew that literary merit did not guarantee success in the examination hall and that luck played a part.
曾国藩也知道『场中莫论文』，考试要碰运气，

Yet official distinction remained an obsession, and his expectations were too pressing; he constantly accused his younger son of not studying hard enough.
但功名这念，横亘胸中；期望亦未免过切，总说他的次子不用功。

Jihong’s luck was indeed poor.
偏偏运气也真坏，

When Zeng died, he was still only a provincial graduate, and he never subsequently obtained the metropolitan degree.
直到曾国藩去世，始终是个举人，以后也一直没有能够中进士，

His circumstances differed so greatly from his elder brother’s that he died despondent in the capital.
与长兄相较，境遇大不相同，以至于在京郁郁以终，

It was Zuo who attended to his affairs after his death.
身后还是左宗棠替他料理的。


Compared with Jihong, his sisters fared worse still.
比起曾纪鸿来，他的姐妹们的境遇，又更不如他了，

Some had fierce mothers-in-law; others had worthless husbands.
有的婆婆太凶，有的丈夫没出息。

Zeng governed his household strictly.
曾国藩持家极严，

He said he had seen many daughters of prominent families who clung to the wealth of their parents’ homes and neglected their duties as wives and daughters-in-law, and that none had come to a good end.
说他见过许多名门之女，贪恋母家富，往往不肯在夫家尽子妇之道，到后来都无好结果，

Although his own daughters had made unfortunate marriages, he would not permit them to return home.
因此他的女儿虽都遇人不淑，但因曾国藩不许她们归宁，

They had to endure their misery with their husbands’ families, spending their days in tears.
只好在夫家受罪，个个都是终日以泪洗面。

The fourth daughter had married well, only to be widowed young.
其中四小姐嫁得不错，偏又青年守寡，

Zeng often said that his luck in sons-in-law was poor.
所以曾国藩生前常说，他的『坦运不佳』。

The sixth daughter, his youngest—what Hunan people called the “last little miss”—was Zeng Jifen.
六小姐是取小的女儿，湖南人称为『满小姐』，名叫曾纪芬，

She married only after his death.
她是曾国藩去世后才嫁的。

Her uncle, Ninth Marshal Zeng, had arranged the match with the Nie family of Hengshan, and the wedding was set for the eleventh year of Tongzhi.
本来由她叔叔『九帅』作媒，许婚于衡山聂家，定在同治十一年出阁。

But early in the second month of that year, Zeng suffered a stroke and died in office as governor-general of Liangjiang.
不意就在这年二月初，曾国藩中风殁于两江总督任上；

By the time mourning ended, the Guangxu reign had begun.
到得服满已是光绪年间。


Jifen’s husband, Nie Guiji, whose courtesy name was Yuntai, belonged to an established Hengshan family long known for charitable works.
曾纪芬的夫婿聂规缉，字芸台，他家是衡山世家，先世以行善出名。

He had failed even to gain the provincial degree and could obtain only minor employment.
但聂规缉却连个举人都没有考上，以致于只能混个小差使；

One of his brothers-in-law had been made director of the Defence Preparations Bureau by the former governor-general of Liangjiang, Liu Kunyi.
他有个姐夫为先前的两江总督刘坤一委为『筹防局总办』，

Nie followed him to Jiangning alone and took a position in the bureau, receiving only eight taels for transport expenses.
聂规缉单身跟到江宁，在筹防局当差，只得八两银子的车马费，

Yet he wanted to bring his wife there.
但却要接眷；

Once in Jiangning, he had discovered how widely Zeng’s former pupils and subordinates were dispersed.
原来聂规缉到了江宁，才知道曾国藩真是门生故吏满天下，

By presenting his wife under the title “Lord Wenzheng Zeng’s youngest daughter,” he could extract considerable benefit from her connections.
将他妻子以『曾文正的满小姐』这个『头衔』搬出来，在裙带上着实能拖出来一点好处，

That was why he wished her to join him.
这就是他接眷的打算。

Following his instructions, Jifen made a special call on the wife of Li Hanzhang, governor-general of Huguang, when her boat from Hunan passed through Wuchang.
果然，曾纪芬照她丈夫的嘱咐，由湖南坐船经武昌时，特为去拜见湖广总督李瀚章的夫人，

She said a little about her husband’s circumstances.
稍为谈一谈丈夫的境况，

Nie was promptly appointed the Hunan Transport Supervision Bureau’s representative in Jiangning, with a monthly allowance of fifty taels.
聂规缉立即被委为湖南督运局驻江宁的委员，月支津贴五十两，

Life became quite comfortable.
日子过得很舒服了。


Soon after succeeding Liu Kunyi at Jiangning, Zuo invited Jifen to the governor-general’s residence to talk over old times.
及至左宗棠接刘坤一的手，到了江宁不久，便将曾纪芬接到总督衙门叙旧，

Zeng had been born in the xinwei year, the sixteenth of Jiaqing; Zuo, born in the following renshen year, was a year younger and assumed the role of her uncle.
曾国藩生在嘉庆十六年辛未；左宗棠生在壬申小一岁，因而以叔父自居。

After Zeng Guoquan captured Jiangning, Zuo and Zeng Guofan had quarrelled and ceased corresponding for three or four years.
左宗棠在曾国荃克江宁后，与曾国藩失和，有三四年不通音问，

But when Zuo was ordered to campaign in the west, Zeng sent Liu Songshan of the Xiang Army to assist him.
但当左示棠奉命西征，曾国藩命湘军刘松山相助，

His help proved invaluable and deeply moved Zuo.
大为得力，这使得左宗棠大为感动，

Moreover, the decisive opportunity in Zuo’s career had come when Zeng recognized his ability and entrusted him with independent command to recover Zhejiang, enabling him to receive a noble title alongside the Zeng brothers.
而况平生功名，关键所在是曾国藩知道他的才具，派他独当一面收复浙江，与曾氏兄弟同时封爵。

Having risen to the highest ministerial honours and a marquisate, Zuo could hardly forget the source of his good fortune.
拜相封侯，位极人臣，饮水思源，亦不能不感激曾国藩；

Outwardly he remained as stubborn as ever, criticizing Zeng at every turn, but privately his attitude had changed greatly.
所以表面上倔强如昔，仍旧处处要批评曾国藩，私底下的态度，却已大为改变，

When Zeng died, Zuo sent a funeral couplet whose first line read: “In loyalty to the state and discernment of men, I acknowledge myself inferior to the chief minister.”
曾国藩殁后，他致送的挽联，道是∶『谋国之忠，知人之明，自愧不如元辅』，

This amounted to conceding defeat—an uncommon act for a man of Zuo’s temperament.
这等于认输，以左宗棠的性情来说，是很难得的事。


His care for Zeng’s descendants was intended to bear out the couplet’s second line: “Our shared purpose was firm as metal; our corrections of each other, a whetstone; may neither betray the hopes of a lifetime.”
至于照应曾国藩的后人，是为了要证实他的挽联中的下一句∶『同心若金，攻错若石，相期无负平生』，

Their disagreements concerned affairs of state and had never impaired their private friendship.
与曾国藩是为国事而争，私交丝毫无损。

Elderly men, moreover, often regarded a friend’s daughter as a precious child of their own.
特别是老年人，往往有一种将朋友的女儿看作自己掌上珠的通性，

Zuo’s affection extended to Nie.
爱屋及乌，对聂规缉亦就另眼相看，

He appointed him to the military administration office and invariably summoned him to share the midday meal.
派了他营务处的差使，每天中午会食，一定找聂规缉；

He approved of Nie’s willingness to speak honestly and his interest in Western learning, and intended to foster his career.
对他的肯说实话、留心西学，颇为赞许，有心要培植他。

Nie accompanied him on this tour of military inspection outside the province.
这回左宗棠出省阅兵，聂规缉作随员，

Li Mianlin knew the young man, and Zuo deliberately asked, “Mianlin, do you know Nie Yuntai well?”
李勉林跟他是熟人，左宗棠故意相问∶『勉林，你跟聂芸台熟不熟？』

Li, whose personal name was Xingrui, had once managed military supplies for Zeng.
李勉林各州兴锐，早年曾替曾国藩办过粮台，

“He is Lord Wenzheng’s youngest son-in-law,” he replied.
当即答道∶『他是曾文正的满女婿，

“Of course I know him well.”
我当然很熟。』

“Excellent.
『那就再好没有。

You seem very busy.
我看你也很忙，

I should like to appoint him your assistant director.”
我想派他来当你的会办。』



胡雪岩 · 萧瑟洋场
The Desolate Foreign Settlement
第三章（本章第3部分，共4部分）
逐句英中对照
原著：高阳


“Your Excellency’s concern for an old friend and wish to improve Nie Zhongfang’s circumstances deserve our fullest sympathy,” Li replied.
『大人眷念故人，要调剂调剂聂仲芳，这番至意，我们当然要体仰；

“I suggest that we send him fifty taels a month in salary while he continues to serve with you.”
我想，每个月送地五十两银子薪水，仍旧在大人那里当差好了。』

Zuo was astonished.
左宗棠一听愕然，

“What, Mianlin?
『怎么，勉林，』

You do not want Nie Zhongfang?”
他问∶『你不欢迎聂仲芳？』

“I dare not conceal the truth.
『不敢欺大人，

Under Your Excellency’s personal instruction and supervision, he would not step out of line.
聂仲芳在大人那里，亲自教导督责，他不敢越轨；

Here he might revert to his old ways.
到了我这里，也许会故态复萌。

As Lord Wenzheng’s youngest son-in-law, he would be difficult for me to reprimand.
他是曾文正的满女婿，我不便说他，

If public business suffered, it would be bad for everyone.”
耽误了公事，大家不好。』

Zuo had begun to feel angry, but now asked calmly, “What old ways do you mean?”
这一说，原来有些生气的左宗棠，心平气和地问说∶『你说他「故态复萌」，请问，是什么故态？』

“Nie is an idle young gentleman.
『聂仲芳是纨绔，

He is three years younger than the youngest Miss Zeng.
他比满小姐小三岁，

They married in the first year of Guangxu, and by the fourth year, when he was only twenty-four, he had already taken a concubine.”
光绪元年成婚；到光绪四年，才廿四岁，已经娶了姨太太。』

“I know about that.
『这件事我知道，

He sent her away long ago.
他的那个早就遣走了。』

What else?”
左宗棠问∶『还有呢？』


“When Zeng Jiegang was appointed envoy to Britain and France, both Chen Songsheng, the second daughter’s husband, and Nie wanted to accompany him as members of his staff.
『还有，曾劼刚那年奉派出使英、法两国，二小姐的故爷陈松生与聂仲芳都想跟去当随员，

He took Chen but not Nie.
结果劼刚带了陈松生，没有带聂仲芳。

Passing through Shanghai, he explained when I asked why he treated two brothers-in-law differently: ‘Taking him would be a burden.’ He added, ‘Read my diary and you will understand.’” Li continued, “If a close relation by marriage felt that way, Your Excellency, how could I dare employ him?”
劼刚路过上海的时候，我问他同为妹婿，何以厚此薄彼。劼刚说∶我带了他去是个累。又说∶』你看了我的日记就知道了。『李勉林又说∶』他们郎舅至亲，尚且如此，大人倒想，我怎么敢用他？

“Did you read Jiegang’s diary?”
『『喔，』左宗棠问∶『你看了劼刚的日记没有呢？』

“I did.”
『看了。』

“What did it say?”
『日记中怎么说？』

“I copied it.
『我录得有副本，

I shall send you the copy later.”
回头送来给大人看。』

“Good.
『好！

Please let me see it.”
请你送来我看看。』


As soon as Li returned, he had the copy of Zeng Jiegang’s diary specially delivered to the Temple of the Heavenly Empress.
李勉林答应着，一回去马上将曾劼刚日记的副本，专程送到天后宫行辕。

With nothing to occupy him that evening, Zuo read it carefully by lamplight.
左宗棠灯下无事，细细看了一遍，

Two entries criticized Nie Guiji.
其中有两条对聂规缉的批评不好，

The first, dated the thirteenth day of the second month in the fourth year of Guangxu, read: “A letter from home reports that Nie Zhongfang has become exceedingly unreasonable.
一条记于光绪四年二月十三日∶『接家报，知聂仲芳乖张已甚，

My youngest sister has suffered unwarranted humiliation and ill-treatment.
季妹横被凌折，

I am deeply troubled and distressed.”
忧闷之至。』

This was a domestic matter, which even an upright magistrate found hard to judge.
这是家务，清官难断，

The other entry, dated the fifteenth day of the ninth month that year, explained why Zeng would not take Nie: “After luncheon, I wrote to my brother-in-law Nie Zhongfang declining his request to go abroad.
另外有一条记于当年九月十五日，说他不用聂仲芳的原因∶『午饭后，写一函答妹婿聂仲芳，阻其出洋之请，

To take Songsheng and refuse Zhongfang, when both are my brothers-in-law, is certain to arouse resentment.
同为妹婿，挈松生而阻仲芳，将来必招怨恨，

Yet this is a journey of ten thousand miles and no private undertaking of mine.
然而万里远行，又非余之私事，

I cannot give way to family feeling and make an irresponsible accommodation.
势不能徇新戚之情面，苟且迁就也。

Among my friends, few equal Songsheng in character, capacity, and learning.
松生德器学识，朋友中实罕其匹，

His presence will benefit the mission.
同行必于使事有益。

Zhongfang is young and much too steeped in the habits of a pampered idler.
仲芳年轻而纨绔习气太重，

Beyond social accomplishments, he has no particular ability.
除应酬外，乃无一长，

He is also unstable in temperament, with unpredictable changes of mood.
又性根无定，喜怒无常，

How could I burden myself with him?
何可携以自累，

I have therefore firmly refused.”
是以毅然辞之。』

Zuo reflected that none of these faults was incurable.
左宗棠心想，这不是什么不可救药的毛病。

If Nie had been as Zeng Jize described him then, the absence of those faults now merely showed that over the past three or four years he had worked to correct them and improve himself.
如果当时聂规缉如曾纪泽所言，现在看来却无此毛病，正好说明此人三四年以来，力矫前失，肯求上进。

Li had many failings in his management of the arsenal and feared that Nie would notice them.
李勉林在制造局有许多毛病，怕落在聂规缉眼中，

He was using Zeng Jiegang as a shield.
故而拿曾劼刚作挡箭牌，

There was no need to take him seriously.
不必理他。


His mind was made up, but he had to leave for Jiangning the next day and could not discuss the matter with Li in person.
主意虽定，但因第二天便须启程江宁，无法与李勉林面谈，

He therefore wrote a letter himself: “Lord Wenzheng used to laugh at his own poor luck in sons-in-law and approved of few among them.
因而亲自执笔写了一封信说∶『曾文正尝自笑坦运不佳，于诸婿中少所许可，

Even Jihong did not greatly please him.
即纪鸿亦不甚得其欢心，

Jiegang alone won his approval, yet even with him he feared that intelligence was too openly displayed.
其所许可者，只劼刚一人，而又颇忧其聪明太露，

No doubt he had grounds for this judgment.
此必有所见而云然。

We, however, must not make such distinctions in our treatment of his descendants.
然吾辈待其后昆，不敢以此稍形轩轾。

Last year, while staying in the capital, I saw Jihong’s distress and poverty and was deeply moved.
上年弟在京寓，目睹纪鸿苦窘情状，不觉慨然，

I arranged funds for his medicines, burial clothes and coffin, and the return of his remains to his native place.
为谋药饵之资，殡殓衣棺及还丧乡里之费，

I made no adverse distinction.
亦未尝有所歧视也。

Jiegang’s letter of thanks from London was most earnest; one may infer that he too would not lightly indulge in partiality or dislike among his own kin.
劼刚在伦敦致书言谢，却极拳拳，是于骨肉间不敢妄生爱憎厚薄之念，亦概可想。

Why should Zhongfang alone be an exception?
兹于仲芳，何独不然。

What appears in the diary was a momentary lapse of discretion on Jiegang’s part and must not be taken as a final judgment.”
日记云云，是劼刚一时失检，未可据为定评。』

At this point Zuo felt that he was forcing the argument.
写到这里，自觉有些强词夺理；

Given his position, it amounted to using authority to overbear Li.
以他的地位，便是仗势欺人，

He paused in thought and devised a more defensible case.
所以凝神细想了一会，想出一番说得过去的道理。

“Tradition says: ‘Remembering the man, we cherish even his tree.
『传曰∶』思其人犹爱其树，

A gentleman’s affections should be generous.’
君子用情，惟其厚焉「，

Viewed thus, your treatment of Zhongfang presents no difficulty.
以此言之，阁下之处仲芳不难，

A bureau employee is not the same as a regular official, nor bureau work the same as the government of a jurisdiction.
局员非官僚之比；局务非政事之比。

If he is capable, advance him; if incapable, remove him.
仲芳能则进之，不能则撤之，

If he commits no fault, allow him his place; if he does err, criticize and expose the fault.
其幸而无过也容之，不幸而有过则攻之讦之，

Let him feel both encouragement and warning, so that hope, resolve, and apprehension may stir him to achievement rather than leave him discarded as useless material.
俾有感奋激励之心，以生其鼓欣鼓舞、激励震惧之念，庶仲芳有所成就，不至弃为废材，

In treating Zhongfang thus, you will have fulfilled your obligation to Lord Wenzheng.”
而阁下有以处仲芳，即有以对曾文正矣。

Zuo felt that this was forthright and reasonable, allowing fully for both principle and affection.
『左宗棠自觉这段话说得光明正大，情理周至，

Yet something remained to be said, and he added: “My friendship with Lord Wenzheng began very early.
但意思还不足，因而又添了一段∶』弟与文正论交最早，

Our mutual sincerity was known to all; so too was our estrangement in later years.
彼此推诚相与，天下所共知；晚岁凶终隙末，亦天下所共见，

Yet since his death, I have treated his sons, his brother, and his relatives and friends exactly as I did while he lived.
然文正逝后，待文正之子若弟，及其亲友，无异文正之生存也。

Do you consider that right, or not?”
阁下以为然耶否耶？『


After seeing Zuo off, Li had scarcely returned to the arsenal when the letter arrived, together with the diary copy.
送走了左宗棠，李勉林刚回制造局，便收到了左宗棠的信及送还的曾纪泽的日记。

Its lofty reasoning not only insisted on the original proposal but implicitly reproached him for refusing to care for Nie, sowing discord between close relations, and failing to repay Zeng’s earlier patronage.
信上一篇大道理，不但坚持原意，而且隐隐责备他，不肯照顾聂规缉，反而离间人家郎舅至亲的感情，对不起曾国藩生前栽培之德。

Li was naturally displeased.
李勉林自然很不高兴。

Yet there was nothing he could do.
没有法子！

It was not high office that one feared, he reflected, but the authority directly over oneself.
他心里在想，不怕官，只怕管；

Zuo had the power to appoint Nie assistant director; writing to explain his decision was a courtesy.
左宗棠要派聂规缉来当会办，是他的职权，写信解释，还是客气的做法。

Then another thought occurred to him.
接下来又想，

Zuo valued Nie because he spoke honestly and attended to Western learning.
左宗棠赏识聂规缉，是因为他肯说实话，而且肯留心『西学』，

He could hardly be ignorant of the arsenal’s shipbuilding and weapons manufacture.
不用说，制造局造船造枪械，他不会是外行；

A knowledgeable man willing to speak the truth would discover its many discreditable secrets.
不是外行又肯说实话，制造局的许多见不得人的内慕，就瞒不住了。

Perhaps Zuo was sending him precisely to find fault with its director.
左宗棠派此人来当会办，说不定就是专门来捉他的毛病的。


The thought weighed upon Li, but he had to pull himself together and respond.
这样转着念头，不免心事重重，但还是得强打精神来应付，

He summoned his trusted drafting and administrative staff, announced Nie’s forthcoming appointment, and instructed the drafting officer to prepare a formal request for it, in courteous and flattering terms.
当即将亲信的文案、庶务都找了来，宣布聂规缉即将来当会办，关照文案备禀请派任的公事，措词要客气、要夸奖。

He then gave the administrative officer two orders: find a spacious residence for the assistant director and furnish it splendidly; and send someone to Jiangning with three months’ salary to escort “Assistant Director Nie” and his wife to their new post.
然后交代庶务两件事∶第一、替会办找个宽敞的公馆，陈设布置，务求华美；第二，派专人携带三个月的薪水，到江宁去接『聂会办』夫妇来上任。

This officer, Wang Boyan, was Li’s confidant.
这个厂务叫王伯炎，是李勉林的心腹，

Although nominally responsible for administrative matters, he did far more than attend to routine details.
名为厂务，并不只管制造局的冗杂小事，

As an adviser he could intervene in engineering and purchasing, and as Li’s strategist he could offer suggestions whenever necessary.
他不但顾问可以干预工程及购料，甚至还是李勉林的智囊，随时可以提出建议；

He was also Li’s eyes and ears, closely following outside criticism of the arsenal.
当然，他也是李勉林的耳目，外界对制造局的批评，一直很注意的。

Reporting that the arrangements had been made, he brought up Focke.
将李勉林交代的事，办妥了来复命时，王伯炎提到福克，

“Do you intend to negotiate the contract with Focke yourself, Director, or wait for Assistant Director Nie?”
『跟福克的那张合约，』他问∶『总办是打算自己跟他谈呢，还是等聂会办来谈？』

“What do you think?”
『你看呢？』


“That depends on your wishes.
『这要看总办的意思。』

Each course has advantages.
王伯炎说∶『各有各的好处。

If we wait for Nie, His Excellency will be thoroughly gratified, and Nie will be pleased too.
等聂会办来谈，好处是左大人的面子十足，聂会办也很高兴，

Moreover, if Nie takes a personal profit, you will have something to hold over him and need never fear his disobedience.”
而且，聂会办如果弄了好处，就有个把柄在总办手里，以后不怕他不就范。』

“And the disadvantage?”
『嗯、嗯！』李勉林问∶『坏处呢？』

“That he may take no profit.
『坏处就是他不要好处。

Then a precedent will have been established: all such contracts will be negotiated by him, and your authority will pass into other hands.”
公事上是开了个例，以后这种合约都归他来谈，总办的大权旁落了。』

Li considered. “Newly arrived, he certainly will not dare take anything.
『李勉林想了一下答说∶』他刚刚来，决不敢弄好处，

He will give us no hold over him; we shall merely establish an unfortunate precedent.” “Exactly.
不会有把柄落在我们手里；反而开了个恶例『』说得是。

Your present course is very wise: be as courteous as possible, make him comfortable in every way, but give him no real authority and little public business to attend to.”
总办的做法也很高明，尽量跟他客气，敷衍得他舒舒服服；就是不给他实权，叫他少管公事。

“Yes.
『』对！

I leave it to you to keep him comfortable.
怎么把他敷衍得舒舒服服，就交给你办了；

A few extra taels do not matter.”
大不了多花几两银子，不要紧。

“Very well.
『』是！

Focke asked yesterday when we could discuss the contract.
『王伯炎答说∶』福克昨天来问道，什么时候谈合约，

I said that while His Excellency was here you had no time, and that we must wait until he left.
我说这两天左大人在这里，总办没有工夫，等左大人走了再说。

I shall now tell him to come at once.”
现在我就通知他了，叫他马上来谈。

“Good.
『』好！

You negotiate with him.”
你跟他谈。『


Focke had long since prepared everything: specifications, prices, delivery dates, and a draft contract.
福克是早就预备好了的，品类、价格、交货期限，合约底稿；

Prices depended on quantity—the larger the purchase, the cheaper each item—but the commission was calculated at the full agreed percentage.
价格是照数量多寡决定，买得愈多愈便宜，但佣金却照比例实足计算。

Commissions on arms varied, though twenty per cent was the minimum.
军火的佣金，高低不等，但最少也得一个二八扣，

Focke, however, offered only ten.
不过福克开的佣金，只得一个折扣；

Wang Boyan smiled at the interpreter. “After so many years in China, why does Mr Focke speak like a novice?”
王伯炎便向翻译笑道∶『福克先生在中国多年，怎么说外行话？』

“Is the commission rate wrong?”
『是，是佣金的折扣不对？』

“No.
『不是佣金的折扣不对。』

He is treating us as novices.”
王伯炎又换了一个说法∶『是拿我们当外行看。』

The interpreter conferred with Focke for a while, then turned back. “Mr Focke says that, because His Excellency personally instructed him to undertake this transaction, he has kept the price exceptionally low.
翻译跟福克叽哩咕噜谈了一阵，转脸向王伯炎说道∶『福克的意思是，这笔生意因为是面奉左大人交代，价钱格外克已，

He has quoted at cost and is effectively doing the work for nothing.
所以他是照成本开的，等于白当差；

He asks you to understand.”
要请王老爷原谅。』

“He is too kind!
『言重，言重！』

It is we who must ask his understanding.
王伯炎说∶『我们要请他原谅，

How am I to account to my superiors for such a figure?
这个数目，我怎么向上头交代？

Does he offer Mr Hu the same rate?”
莫非他跟胡大先生做交易，也是这个折扣？』


“Yes,” Focke actually replied through the interpreter, though he added an explanation.
『是的，「福克居然透过翻译，这样回答；不过他也有解释，』

“When I negotiated directly with Mr Hu, any terms could be discussed.
以前如果跟胡先生自己谈。什么话都好说；

But when I dealt personally with His Excellency Zuo, Mr Hu took no rebate at all.”
倘或是跟左大人自己谈，胡先生是连一个回扣都不要的。

“Well, well!”
『』唏！唷！

Wang made a great show of surprise.
『王伯炎大惊小怪地，』

“Then he is granting us a special favour?”
照这样说，他还算特为照应我们的？

“That is not quite what he means,” the interpreter answered. “As we understand it, rebates vary with circumstances.
『『话也不是这么说。』翻译答说∶『据我们所知，回扣有多有少，看情形而定；

There will be more business later, and opportunities to make up for this.”
好在以后还有生意，总有补报的时候。』

“This is our first transaction.
『我是头一回，

He ought to let me make a respectable showing.
总要让我有个面子，

Tell him I shall make it up to him next time.”
你跟他说，我下一回补报他。』

The interpreter spoke with Focke at length, then returned helplessly to Wang. “Mr Focke says any rebate can be arranged, but the price must rise accordingly.”
翻译跟福克又是谈了好半天，最后无可奈何地回复王伯炎，『王老爷，』他说∶『福克的意思，回扣多少都行，不过价钱要提高。』

“To what figure?”
『提高到多少呢？』

“That depends on you.
『这要看王老爷，

Whatever amount you wish.”
要多少就是多少。』

“Ah, he means to put a hat on the price?”
『喔，他的意思是「戴帽子」？』

“Yes.”
『是的。』


“And will he stand by the price with its hat on?”
『那末戴了帽子他承认不承认呢？』

“Certainly.
『当然承认。

But…” The interpreter faltered.
不过┅┅』那翻译吞吞吐吐地没有再说下去。

“But what?” Wang demanded.
王伯炎当然要追问，『不过什么？』

“This is our first transaction.
他说∶『大家头一回做交易，

We must be frank with each other.”
要以诚相待。』

“Then to be frank, the price list has already been sent out.”
『那末，我说老实话，价目表早就开出去了。』

“To whom?”
『开给哪个？』

“Mr Hu.”
『胡大先生。』

The interpreter hastily added, “Not just within the last few days.”
翻译赶紧又补了一句∶『不是这两天的事。』

Wang was furious.
王伯炎一听这话，大为光火；

His face went from ashen to crimson before he finally uttered the words: “So it is a trap!”
脸色青一阵、红一阵的，最后吐出一句话来∶『原来是个圈套！』


The meeting broke up unpleasantly.
当下弄得不欢而散，

Further inquiries gave the indignant Wang fresh cause for anger.
王伯炎愤愤不平，再一打听，还有气人的事，

Determined to preserve his good relationship with Hu, Focke had reserved a ten-per-cent share for him in the commission on this transaction.
原来福克决意跟胡雪岩保持良好的关系，所以在这笔军火的佣金中，为他保留了一个折扣；

Hu had said he did not wish to profit without doing the work, but Focke persisted in his original plan.
虽然胡雪岩表示，不愿不劳而获，但福克还是照原来的计划。

Twenty per cent was the minimum customary rebate on arms; now half of it was to be given away to someone else for nothing.
买军火两成回扣，是最起码的行情，还要平白为人分去一半，

Wang could scarcely explain this to his director.
王伯炎觉得这件事对总办实在很难交代。

Li already felt he had been duped.
李勉林本来就有上当的感觉，

In his view, had Hu introduced Focke to Zuo, he would have been intervening in Jiangnan arms procurement in his capacity as an officer of the Western Expedition Transport Bureau.
在他的判断，胡雪岩将福克带到左宗棠那里，是以西征转运局委员的身份干预江南的军火采办事宜，

A censor’s impeachment could have embarrassed even Zuo.
京中的『都老爷』参上一本，连左宗棠的面子都不好看，

That was why they had sent Focke to seek Li’s introduction.
因而叫福克来请他引见。

In fact, Li supposed, they had settled everything privately and merely used him to ferry the business across.
事实上他们暗底下都谈好了，只是利用他来摆个渡而已。


After Wang’s report, Li considered the matter serious enough to consult Shao Youlian, the Shanghai intendant.
因此听到王伯炎的报告以后，认为事态很严重，特意去找上海道邵友濂商量。

“Li Hongzhang’s mourning has come at a most unfortunate time.
『合肥道赵丁忧，实在不凑巧，

In Beiyang, Zhang Zhenxuan plainly intends to replace him.
北洋是张振轩大有取而代之的意思；

Here, Zuo advances at every step.
这里左湘阴着着进逼，

Nie Zhongfang is planted inside, and Hu Xueyan contrives one scheme after another outside.
里面一个聂仲芳卧底；外面一个胡雪岩花样百出。

The arsenal is the foundation of Beiyang’s strength; I fear we shall lose it.”
制造局是北洋的基础，看来要保不住了。』

Deeply anxious, he appealed to Shao. “Brother Xiaocun, you are always resourceful.
李勉林忧心忡忡地说∶『小村兄，你一向足智多谋，

For the sake of our common debt to Lord Wenzheng, you must help me.”
总要看在大家都是曾文正一脉相传这一点的情份上，帮帮我的忙才好。』

“You need not speak so gravely.
『言重，言重。』

Our fortunes are bound together; I could never stand by.
号『小村』的邵友濂说∶『彼此休戚相关，我决无坐视之理。

Hu carries much less weight with Zuo than he once did.
胡雪岩在左湘阴面前的分量，也大不如前了，

Grit your teeth and hold on while I find an opportunity to strike him from behind so hard that he cannot get up again.”
你先咬咬牙撑住，等我找个机会，好好来打他一闷棍，叫他爬不起来。』

“A hundred-footed creature does not stiffen even in death—” “Even if it does not, it can do nothing more,” Shao interrupted. “The first priority, Brother Mianlin, is to keep Nie Zhongfang comfortable.”
『百足之虫，死而不僵。』『即使不僵也不能有什么作为了。』邵友濂打断他的话说∶『勉林兄，目前最要紧的一件事，你要把聂仲芳敷衍好。』

“I understand.”
『我明白。』

“As for Focke’s contract, you had better let Hu sign it with him.”
『至于福克的合约，你最好还是让胡雪岩跟他去订。』

“Is there a particular reason?”
『喔，这，这有什么讲究吗？』

“Naturally.
『自然有讲究。

This money will ultimately have to come from the Shanghai Customs receipts.
这笔经费，将来少不得要在江海关的收入之中开支；

Suppose I cannot arrange the funds—would I not be exposing you to his demands?”
如果我这里调度不开，不是害你受人家的逼？』

After reflection, Li understood.
李勉林沉吟了一会，恍然大悟，

Shao controlled the customs revenue and could make excuses to delay payment.
江海关的税收归邵友濂管，将来该付福克的款子，他可以借故拖延；

If Hu had signed the contract, Focke could only ask Hu to intervene.
如果是胡雪岩跟福克签的约，福克自然只能找胡雪岩去办交涉，

By obstructing Focke, Shao would really be making difficulties for Hu.
所以邵友濂的刁难福克，实际上便是与胡雪岩为难。

“Excellent!” Li agreed.
『好，好！』等想通了，李勉林满口应承，

“I shall attend to it as soon as I return.”
『我回去就办。』


Li instructed Wang to prepare a report to Zuo stating that Focke’s price was too high and negotiations had failed.
李勉林的办法是，命王伯炎备公事禀报左宗棠，说福克索价过高，合约谈不拢，

Since Focke had previously supplied the western expedition and only Hu could make him accept terms, the public interest required that Zuo order Hu directly to conclude the contract.
福克以前承办西征军火，只有胡雪岩能使他就范，所以为了大局着想，请左宗棠径饬胡雪岩与福克签订合约，

The report added that Focke had offered a ten-per-cent rebate, which the Jiangnan Arsenal could not possibly accept; it should therefore be deducted from the price, ensuring that every last fraction went to the public treasury.
同时，福克原拟致送回扣一成，江南制造局决不敢领这笔回扣，请在价款中扣除，庶符涓滴归公之议。

This impeccably proper-sounding report reached the governor-general’s office in Jiangning.
这一份『禀帖』说得冠冕党皇，到得两江总督衙门，

Zuo found it reasonable and sent a copy to Hu with instructions to act.
左宗棠议为言之有理；便将原禀录了一个副本，一并寄交胡雪岩办理。

Thus the affair travelled in a great circle, from Shanghai to Jiangning, from Jiangning to Hangzhou, and from Hangzhou back to Shanghai.
这样由上海而江宁，由江宁而杭州，再由杭州而上海一个大圈子兜下来，

Amid the exchange of letters and telegrams, two months quickly passed.
函电往来，很快地两个月过去，

The transaction remained unsettled, while the wider situation changed profoundly.
事情尚无结果，局势却有了重大变化。


Civil disorder had broken out in Korea to the east.
原来东邻朝鲜发生内乱，

King Yi Hui was weak, and Queen Min wielded power.
国王李熙暗弱，王妃闵氏当权；

The king’s own father, Yi Haeung, known as the Daewongun, had long been struggling with the queen for control.
李熙的本生父叫李癵应，称号是『大院君』，与王妃争权，已非一日，

His followers now attacked the palace, wounded the queen, and killed ministers including Min Gyeom-ho.
这一次的内乱是大院君的党羽进攻王宫，伤及王妃，并杀大臣闵谦镐等人。

Japan seized the opportunity to send troops to Korea.
日本见有机可乘，出兵朝鲜；

Li Shuchang, China’s envoy in Japan, urgently telegraphed acting Governor-General Zhang Shusheng, recommending that Beiyang warships be dispatched immediately to counter the Japanese.
驻日公使黎庶昌急电署直隶总督张树声，建议北洋立派兵舰，与日军抗衡。

Zhang had been eager for a conspicuous achievement.
张树声本就想有声有色地大干一番，

On receiving the warning, he decided to send troops to watch developments while simultaneously reporting to the court.
接到黎庶昌告警的电报，决定一面出兵观变，一面奏报朝廷。

The court commended his prompt response.
朝廷对张树声能够迅速应变，颇为嘉许，

But with France also threatening Vietnam, it feared that the Korean crisis would exceed Zhang’s capacity.
但因法国其时正在图谋越南；朝鲜又有警报，怕张树声无法应付，

Li Hongzhang was therefore ordered to interrupt his mourning at home and return to Tianjin at once.
所以决定命在籍守制的李鸿章夺情复起，即日回津。

Someone advised Zhang that, since the court had appointed Li to direct the matter, he should wait until Li resumed office before sending troops.
因而便有人劝张树声说∶『朝中既已命令他主持此事，出兵似以等合肥回任后再办为宜。』

Zhang refused.
张树声不听，

Speed was essential in war; if the opportunity were lost and Japan acted first, China would be at a disadvantage.
说兵贵神速，时机一误，让日本军着了先鞭，中国要落下风。

Responsible as he was for Beiyang, he could not allow indecision to lead him astray.
他即负北洋重任，不能因循自误。


Thus, when the second telegram urging Li to depart had only just reached Hefei, and Li had replied that he would leave immediately for Tianjin by way of Shanghai, Zhang’s expedition was already crossing the sea eastward.
于是当第二道催李鸿章动身的电报刚到合肥，李鸿章已复奏即行就道，由上海转天津时，张树声所派的军队，已经在『跨海征东』途中了。

Its naval and military commanders were Ding Ruchang, a Beiyang naval officer registered for appointment as commander-in-chief, and Wu Changqing, nominally commander-in-chief of the Guangdong navy but in practice a land commander.
张树声所派水陆两员大将，一个是北洋水师记名提督丁汝昌；一个是广东水师提督吴长庆，此人名在水师，实在是陆军，

Wu was a veteran of the Huai Army stationed at Dengzhou in Shandong.
他是淮军宿将，驻扎山东登州；

He sailed from there in China Merchants’ steamers with six battalions.
随带淮军六营，由登州坐招商局的轮船出海，

His headquarters contained many able men.
幕府中人材济济，

Directing the field military administration was a twenty-four-year-old from an established Jianghuai family: Yuan Shikai, nephew of Yuan Baoheng, the former Hanlin scholar who had risen to vice-minister of revenue and managed supplies for Zuo.
总理前敌营务处的，是一个年方二十四岁的江淮世家子弟，就是翰林出身、官至户部侍郎、曾为左宗棠办过粮台的哀保恒的侄子袁世凯。

Yuan Shikai had disliked study from childhood.
袁世凯从小不喜读书，

Despite his distinguished family, his disreputable behaviour had made him an outcast among his neighbours.
虽是世家子弟，行为无赖，不齿于乡党。

Unable to remain at home, he conceived an extraordinary plan: gathering more than ten unemployed youths, he travelled from Xiangcheng in Henan to Yantai in Shandong.
在家乡存不住身，异想天开，召集了无业少年十余人，由河南项城到山东烟台，

Leaving his companions at an inn, he went alone to see Wu.
将同伴留在旅舍中，只身去见吴长庆。

Wu, then handling military affairs in Shandong under his Guangdong naval title, had been a sworn brother of Yuan’s adoptive father, Yuan Baoqing.
吴长庆当时以广东水师提督办理山东军务，他跟袁世凯的嗣父袁保庆是八拜之交，

He naturally wished to help his old friend’s son and first asked what had brought him there.
对故人之子，当然要照应，首先动问来意。



胡雪岩 · 萧瑟洋场
The Desolate Foreign Settlement
第三章（本章第4部分，共4部分）
逐句英中对照
原著：高阳


“As the son of a military family, I have laid down the writing brush to take up arms,” Yuan replied.
袁世凯答说∶『身为将门之子，投笔从戎。』

The dozen or so young men he had brought, he added, were all rare military talents.
又说他带来的十几个少年，都是难得的将才，

“I ask you, Uncle, to employ every one of them.”
『请老伯全数录用。』

Wu was astonished, but could hardly call him absurd or rebuke his presumption.
吴长庆大为诧异，不好骂他荒唐、斥之为冒昧。

Instead, he sent an officer to the inn with banknotes to dismiss his companions kindly and provide their travelling expenses.
当下派了一名军官携带银票，到旅舍里，将他的同伴好言资遣。

Yuan himself was, of course, kept on.
当然，袁世凯是被留下来了。

“Have you gained admission to the county school?”
『你进了学没有？』

“No.”
『没有。』

Yuan was not even a licentiate.
袁世恺连秀才都不是，

He had merely purchased the status of an Imperial Academy student, which entitled him to sit the Shuntian provincial examination in the northern capital.
不过捐了监生，照例可应北闱顺天乡试；

Wu told him to study in camp under Zhang Jian.
吴长庆便叫他在营读书，拜张謇为师。

Known by the courtesy name Jizhi, Zhang was a distinguished scholar of Nantong.
此人号季直，是南通的名士，

Besides advising Wu on military affairs, he tutored Wu’s second son, Wu Baochu.
他在吴长庆幕府中参赞军务，同时也是吴开庆次子吴保初的业师。


Since Yuan was to take the examination, Zhang naturally taught him eight-legged essays.
既然要应考，张謇当然教他做八股文。

Yuan had little interest in them.
袁世恺兴趣缺缺；

But in conversations about current affairs and the management of men, he spoke so cogently that Zhang came to admire him.
但陪着张謇谈谈时事，以及用人驭士的手段，却头头是道，很得张謇的赏识。

Another member of Wu’s staff, Zhu Mingpan, was also from Nantong.
吴长庆幕府中，还有个朱铭盘，也是南通人，

He, Zhang, and the gifted poet Fan Kentang were known as the Three Scholars of Tongzhou.
与张謇及另一个诗做得极好的范肯堂，号称为『通州三生』；

Zhu too liked Yuan.
这朱铭盘对袁世恺亦颇有好感，

When Zhang recommended him, with Zhu supporting the recommendation, Wu appointed him assistant in the military administration office and assigned him two orderlies.
因此，当张謇保荐袁世恺时，而朱铭盘在一旁帮腔以后，吴长庆便委袁为营务处帮办，而且派了两名勤务兵给他。

This occurred in the fourth month of the sixth year of Guangxu, two years before.
这是前年光绪六年四月间的事。

When the Korean disturbances broke out, Zhang Shusheng sent Ding Ruchang specially to summon Wu for consultation.
及至朝鲜发生内乱，张树声派丁汝昌特召吴长庆议事。

Wu took Zhang Jian to Tianjin, where three days of secret discussions produced a plan to suppress the disorder.
吴长庆带同张謇，在天津密商三日，定策平乱。

It was the renwu year—one of the years of the Rat, Horse, Rabbit, or Rooster in which the triennial examinations were held.
这年壬午，『子午犯酉，大比之年』，

Ordered to go to the capital for the provincial examination, Yuan happened also to be in Tianjin.
袁世恺奉命入京乡试，恰好也在天津；

Hearing of the projected Korean expedition, he sought out Zhang Jian and asked to abandon letters for arms, going to Korea instead of the examination.
听说要出兵朝鲜，便去见张謇，想弃文就武，不赴乡试而赴朝鲜。

Zhang agreed to intercede with Wu, and Yuan obtained his wish.
张謇答应了，为他向吴长庆要求，如愿以偿。


After they reached Yantai, Wu returned to Dengzhou to mobilize his troops.
到了烟台以后，吴长庆回登州去调兵遣将，

Zhang Jian was responsible for assigning ships, requisitioning provisions, and assembling supplies at Yantai.
在烟台派船征粮，须备辎重，由张謇负责，

With so many varied tasks, he naturally turned to Yuan for assistance.
事多且杂，张謇顺理成章的找了袁世凯作帮手，

Wu issued him a written appointment to the field military administration, and he found himself entrusted with independent responsibility.
由吴长庆下札子委为『前敌营务处』，居然独当一面了。

At dusk on the twelfth day of the seventh month, Wu’s main force arrived at Incheon from Yantai.
七月十二日黄昏，吴长庆带领大队人马，由烟台抵达朝鲜仁川；

The Japanese land and naval forces, however, had arrived an hour earlier.
可是日本海陆军已经早一小时到达。

As it was already late, both sides remained aboard, intending to land at dawn.
只是天色已晚，中日两军都住在船上，预备天亮登陆。

Then, through the gathering darkness, secret envoys arrived from Queen Min.
哪知就夜色苍茫中，闵妃所遣的密使到了。

Korea’s king, Yi Hui, had succeeded from a collateral branch of the royal house, like the Guangxu emperor.
原来朝鲜国王李熙，也象光绪皇帝一样，是旁支入继；

His biological father, Yi Haeung, the Daewongun, occupied a position comparable to Prince Chun’s, with the difference that the Daewongun served as regent.
李熙的生父『大院君』李是应，便等于醇亲王，所不同的是，『大院君』摄政。


After Yi Hui came of age, the Daewongun resented the situation and struggled with Queen Min for power.
李熙成年以后，『大院君「自然看不过去，便跟闵妃争权。

Like the Empress Dowager Cixi, she was highly capable.
那闵妃象慈禧太后一样，非常能干，

Since Korea was China’s tributary state, she reasoned, wholeheartedly cultivating Chinese officials would give her the advantage.
心想朝鲜是中国的藩属，只要倾心结交中国官吏，自然就占上风，

Japan’s ambitions were growing daily.
此时日本的野心日炽，

Seeing two irreconcilable factions in Korea, it watched for an opportunity that could furnish a pretext for invasion.
看朝鲜两派对立，各不相下，便蓄心要找机会，作为入侵的借口。

At last one arose.
机会终于来了。

Domestic government was neglected, the people were impoverished, and soldiers had gone unpaid for months.
朝鲜内政不修，人民困苦，士兵的饷欠了好几个月，

Repeated protests over their pay produced only incomplete payments, so mutinies and disturbances were frequent.
一再『闹饷』，发又发得不足数，于是便常有造反作乱之事，

The Japanese bought over some of the rebels and deliberately had them plunder the Japanese consulate.
日本人便买通乱党，故意让他们抢劫日本领事馆，

They then prepared to send troops under the pretext of protecting it.
日本便以保护领事馆为名，酝酿出兵朝鲜。

Queen Min learned of this and secretly informed Chinese officials; China’s envoy in Japan also telegraphed Beiyang urgently.
闵妃得到消息，向中国官吏告密；驻日公使亦有急电到北洋，

Both countries sought to arrive first, but their forces reached Korea at virtually the same time.
中日双方军队都想抢个先着，但同时到达，不分先后，

The queen’s envoys changed the situation.
而闵妃的密使一来，情势就不同了。


Meeting Wu and Ding, the envoys said that Japan and the Daewongun were already in collusion.
这些密使谒见吴长庆、丁汝昌，说日本与李癵应已有勾结。

Whichever army reached the capital, Hanseong, first would control the whole situation.
哪一个军队先到朝鲜京城汉城，哪一国便控制了整个局势。

It was like the struggle between Chu and Han, when entry into Xianyang determined the advantage.
这就象楚汉相争，先入咸阳为胜是一样的道理。

“We advise the Celestial Empire’s forces to land under cover of darkness and take a side road to Hanseong.
『为今之计，我们劝天朝大军，乘黑夜登陆，由间道入汉城，

You can reach it in a day and a night.
一昼夜可以抵达。

The Japanese do not know this shortcut.”
这条间道捷径是日本人所不知道的。』

“An excellent idea.
『主意是很好，

But how are the troops to be supplied for that day and night?
可是这一昼夜的供应呢？

They must eat.”
士兵不能不吃饭啊！』

“Do not be concerned.
『请放。』

Everything has been arranged along the route.”
闵妃的密使说∶『沿途都设备好了。』

Delighted, Wu immediately called Zhang Jian and Ma Jianzhong into a secret conference.
吴长庆大喜，立即召集张謇及马建忠密议，

They decided to accept the queen’s plan: five hundred men would land that night, another thousand at dawn, while the rest remained aboard awaiting orders.
决定接受闵妃的计划，先派五百人连夜登陆；另派一千人在黎明下船，其余守在船上待命。

Once the decision was made, Wu assembled his officers in the China Merchants’ steamer’s dining saloon and issued his commands.
密议既定，吴长庆在招商局轮船的大餐间点兵发令。


This should have been an occasion of high spirits and eager volunteers.
这本来应该是士气昂扬、踊跃争先的一个场面，

Instead, after Wu gave his orders, silence lasted for about five minutes.
不过吴长庆下达了命令，肃静无声，约有五分钟之久；

The atmosphere grew painfully strained.
这一下气氛便显得很僵硬了。

At last a deputy battalion commander named Liu approached and spoke quietly. “Our men are land soldiers who have never been to sea.
终于有个姓刘的帮带，凑到吴长庆面前低声说道∶『本营都是陆军，从来没有出过海，

The steamer has only just stopped, and many are seasick.
现在轮船刚停下来，弟兄晕船的很多，

Might you allow them a night’s rest before they go ashore at dawn, Marshal?”
能不能请大帅体谅，让大家休息一夜，到天亮再上岸。』

Wu’s expression changed instantly.
此言一出，吴长庆即时变色，

Worse still, others voiced the same request.
偏偏另外还有同样的请求，

He flew into a rage and struck the table. “At a time and in a place like this, you dare disobey?
吴长庆勃然大怒，拍桌骂道∶『这是什么时候，什么地方，你敢不遵我的命令，

Do you not know military law?”
莫非不知道军法？』

He reached for a command token to order Liu’s execution.
说着，要拔令箭斩那个刘帮带。

Zhang Jian hastily intervened before he could speak again. “Marshal, Liu is no longer fit to lead troops.
张謇在旁，不等他再开口抢着说道∶『大帅，刘帮带不宜再带兵了；

Appoint someone else!”
另外派人吧！』

“Whom?”
『派谁呢？』

“I suggest Yuan Shikai.”
『我看袁世凯可以接替。』

“Very well!”
『好！』

Wu turned to his attendants. “Place Liu under guard.
吴长庆向左右说道∶『把姓刘的先看管起来，

I shall deal with him once the important business is done.”
等我办完了大事再来处置。』


Yuan had meanwhile been summoned.
这时袁世凯已得到通知，

He entered and saluted.
进来行了礼；

“The Marshal has a duty for you,” Zhang told him.
张謇说道∶『大帅有差使派给你，

“Listen carefully.”
你仔细听着。』

Wu took up the command. “Deputy Commander Liu has disobeyed orders.
吴长庆接口下令∶『刘帮带不遵命令，

I have dismissed him and placed him under arrest.
我已把他革职看管，

You are now deputy commander and will take over his men.
现在派你为帮带，接管他的队伍；

Prepare immediately.
即刻预备，

In half an hour, lead one battalion ashore in the boats supplied by the Koreans.
半点钟以后，先领一营人，坐朝鲜派来的船登陆，

Their guides will take you forward on a night march.
由朝鲜向导带领，连夜行军。

Yuan Shikai, can you carry out this assignment?”
袁世凯，这个差使，你担当得下来，担当不下来？』

“I can.”
『能担当。』

“Good.
『好！

If any of your men disobey or violate military law, you may execute them first and report afterwards.”
你部下如有人不遵命，违反军法，准你先斩后报。』

He held out the command token.
说着，吴长庆将手中的令箭，往前一递。

Yuan accepted it and answered loudly, “I obey your orders, Marshal.”
袁世凯接令在手，高声答道∶『遵大帅将令。』

In less than half an hour, he was ready, neatly equipped in short trousers and straw sandals.
半点钟不到，袁世凯已扎束停当，草鞋短裤，干净利落，

He returned to report: “I have settled everything with the Korean interpreter.
进来向吴长庆禀报∶『已经跟朝鲜的译官商量决定，

After landing, we shall march rapidly through the night, take breakfast at Guoshan at dawn, and await Your Excellency there.”
登陆后连夜急行军，天明到果山早饭，在那里恭候大帅驾临。』

Having taken his leave, he immediately went ashore.
辞行既华，立即下船，

At daybreak, Wu followed with two battalions and reached Guoshan at noon.
到得天亮，吴长庆亲统两营，接续前进，中午抵达果山，

Yuan dismounted to greet him.
袁世凯下马迎谒，

He had sent five hundred men ahead under the battalion commander and had remained expressly to await the Marshal.
说已派先锋五百人，由营官率领先走，他特为在此候驾。


“How was the journey?”
『路上怎么样？』

“Entirely peaceful.
『一路平安，

The Koreans have supplied everything we need.
朝鲜的供应很完备，

You may be at ease.”
一切请大帅放心。』

“Good.
『好！』

Anything else to report?”
吴长庆又问∶『还有什么事要报告的？』

“The men’s discipline was poor.
『士兵的纪律不大好，

They plundered the inhabitants and insulted women.
抢民间的东西，还有对妇女无礼，

For an imperial army sent to restore order, such behaviour would earn contempt.
王师戡乱，这样子会让人家看不起，

Acting under your orders, I have executed seven men on the spot.”
世凯已遵大帅将令，就地正法了七个人。』

Wu felt reassured.
一听这话，吴长庆放心了。

He had thought Yuan incapable of commanding troops; now he seemed indeed a worthy descendant of a military family.
原以为他不会带兵，现在看来，倒真不愧将门之后，

Wu commended him and instructed him to continue the advance.
当下慰了一番，关照袁世凯继续前进。


Late that night, the five hundred advance troops reached Hanseong and camped at its south gate.
当天深夜，先锋五百人到了汉城，在南门扎营。

After ten the following morning, Wu arrived at speed with his thousand men and established his main camp at Tunzishan, seven li from the city.
第二天上午十点多钟，吴长庆亲统的一千人亦复疾驰而至，在距汉城七里的屯子山扎下大营，

The Daewongun had learned of their arrival and sent his son, General Yi Jae-myeon, with greetings and gifts for the troops.
其时『大院君』李癵应已经得到消息，派了他的儿子大将军李载冕来见吴长庆，表示慰劳。

Wu responded courteously.
吴长庆亦很客气地敷衍了一番，

Once Yi had left, he immediately entered the city to pay the Daewongun a formal visit.
等李载冕一走，立刻进城去拜访李癵应，作礼貌上的周旋。

Returning to camp, he called his senior officers and advisers into a secret council. Ma Jianzhong proposed seizing the leader to subdue his followers: when the Daewongun returned the visit, they should detain him and send him to Tianjin, intimidating the rebels.
出城回大营以后，吴长庆立即召集高级将领及幕僚密商马建忠建议，擒贼擒王，等李是应来回拜时，设法扣留，送往天津，以寒乱党之胆。

If the rebels still refused pacification, military suppression could follow.
倘或乱党不受安抚，再行进剿。

Wu thought the plan excellent, and everyone agreed.
吴长庆认为此计大妙，其余的人众都同意，

They made their preparations in secret and laid the trap, waiting for the Daewongun to enter it.
于是密密部署，设下了陷阱，只等李癵应来自投。


He returned the visit at four in the afternoon, accompanied by several dozen guards.
李癵应来回拜时，是在下午四点钟，带的卫队有数十名之多；

Received inside the tent, he conversed with Zhang Jian and Ma Jianzhong by exchanging written notes.
接入帐内，由张謇与马建忠二人，与李癵应笔谈，这样交换意见，

Even commonplace civilities took considerable time in this manner.
即令是泛泛的寒暄，一来一往，亦很费事。

Once his guards outside had been separated from him, Wu judged the moment ripe. “By command of the court, I convey an imperial order: Your Highness is to go personally to Beijing and report fully on the rebels.”
等营外李癵应的卫队被隔离开来，看看时候差不多了∶吴长庆便即说道∶『本人奉朝廷之命传旨，着贵藩亲自到北京，面陈乱党的一切。』

Without waiting to discover whether the Daewongun understood, Ma helped him to his feet and took him out of camp.
说完，也不管李癵应听得懂听不懂，由马建忠扶起李癵应出营；

A sedan chair stood ready.
外面有一顶轿子，

They thrust him inside, lifted it, and hurried away.
将他塞入轿内，抬起便走，

More than a hundred picked soldiers escorted him before and behind.
健卒百余人前后夹护，

Through the night and the rain they covered a hundred and twenty li, reaching Namyang harbour early the next morning.
连夜冒雨急驰一百二十里，第二天一早到南阳港口，

Only after he was aboard the warship Weiyuan did the Daewongun understand what had happened.
登上威远兵轮，李是应才知道是怎么回事。


The next target was his eldest son, Yi Jae-myeon, full brother of King Yi Hui, who was said to direct the rebels.
下一个目标是李癵应的长子，亦即韩王李熙的胞兄李载冕，据说，乱党是由他指挥的。

Wu sent Yuan with troops into the city to arrest him, but the rebels themselves had dispersed.
吴长庆派袁世凯领兵入城，逮捕了李载冕，而乱党却已逃散了。

That evening, a secret message from the king told Wu that they were concentrated in two places: Itaewon and Wangxunli.
当天晚上，吴长庆接到李熙的密报，乱党是屯驻在两个地方，一个叫利泰院，一个叫枉寻里。

Wangxunli lay close to Wu’s main camp, so he dealt with it himself.
枉寻里就在吴长庆大营附近，便由他亲自出马；

Yuan was assigned Itaewon.
利泰院的任务派了袁世凯，

A surprise attack in the darkness captured more than a hundred men, while the remaining rabble fled in every direction.
乘黑夜奇袭，抓了一百多人，其余的乌合之众纷纷走避；

Much the same happened at Wangxunli.
枉寻里的情形亦差不多。

By the time three thousand Japanese troops reached Hanseong along the main road, order had already been restored.
等日军三千人沿大路开到汉城，局势已经平定了。

They therefore had no grounds for entering the city and camped outside to avoid a clash with the Qing forces.
这一来，日军便没有进城的理由，为了避免与清军冲突，驻扎在城外。

Japan’s envoy to Korea, Hanabusa Yoshitada, also returned to Hanseong and opened negotiations for compensation.
日本驻韩公使花房义质亦回汉城，向韩国提出赔偿的交涉，

That was not Wu’s concern.
这不是吴长庆的事；
